pages.title: GitHub Actions capture
pages.description: Choose Takeout，regular API export or a chat journal on a temporary GitHub runner．
pages.keywords: github actions capture takeout account export encrypted archive
pages.text: Choose Takeout，regular API export or a chat journal on a temporary GitHub runner． Enable JavaScript to generate a key and decrypt your archive. Full reference Preview available from main . A fork launches a pinned reusable workflow from phishdestroy/TgWitness . The workflow exports an account, selected chats or one chat's event journal using a newly created Telegram session, attests the evidence ZIP or multipart manifest, and uploads only recipient-encrypted handoffs. The normal administration panel is not exposed. Choose client=official_web to run the official-client witness with guarded Telegram Web controls and video．It requires your own upstream proxy and observes one rendered chat．The default client=api retains the full-account export modes described below． The verifier checks the archive against its GitHub attestation, the approved workflow and collector commits, and the signed journal and attachment hashes. The collection process uses pinned upstream code and fresh storage. A reviewer can inspect that code and verify the delivered archive against its recorded run. User flow # The helper explains the five stages and lets you try message or collector substitution on sample data. Start my capture opens the wizard. Choose GitHub Actions capture (preview) on the project homepage, the workspace login screen, or Exports → Open capture helper . You can also open the official helper or tgwitness/static/capture.html from a trusted checkout in a modern browser. The helper makes no network requests for key or file processing. The helper supports the site's interface languages; the temporary collection panel supports English and Russian. Generate a key and save sealed-key.json . This is the only private decryption key. Copy the separate public recipient value. Losing the private key loses access to both the connection and the archive. Confirm that you saved it to unlock the next step. If you already have a delivery file, load the saved key and choose I already have an archive . Fork TgWitness, enable Actions in the fork, and run Sealed chat capture . Paste the public recipient and choose 30, 60, or 120 minutes. Never put a phone number, login code, Telegram password, private key, or session in workflow inputs, commits, issues, or logs. During the run, download sealed-connection from Artifacts and unzip it. Load connection.tgwsealed in the helper, using the saved private key. The resulting link contains a random access secret in its URL fragment. Keep this link private. The panel removes the fragment and keeps the secret in this tab's session storage; it is not placed in HTTP access logs. Open the connection link. Sign in with a QR code, or with your phone number and the login code. Enter your two-step verification password if Telegram asks for it. The built-in API credential pool is used by default, just like the normal workspace. You may expand the optional custom credentials section and enter both api_id and api_hash from my.telegram.org/apps . Leave both fields empty to use the built-in pool; a partial or malformed pair is rejected. Session imports are not allowed. Choose the export mode and scope. The connection link contains an access secret: keep it private. Choose Telegram Takeout , Regular Telegram API or Chat event journal . For account export, choose all accessible chats or load and select one or more chats, then set dates, chat types, account categories and attachment rules. Check settings and size, optionally save the settings JSON for an independent reviewer, then press Start capture . Settings are fixed after starting. Resume works only while this runner exists; finishing early preserves acquired data and records gaps. Deadline expiry after starting produces an explicitly partial archive; expiry before starting or cancellation produces no archive. Wait for sealed-result , download and unzip it, and decrypt delivery.tgwsealed in the helper. You receive delivery.zip , containing evidence.zip , attestation.jsonl , and ins

pages.title: Dedicated account
pages.description: Prepare a separate Telegram account for collection.
pages.keywords: dedicated telegram account session api login
pages.text: Read before you connect an account Use a separate account. Never your main one. Our advice not to use your main account is not a joke. It is reality. Main account Your own app hash: 99% logged out Bans just for low trust are frequent Using it is a really stupid idea Extra account on public pairs Over a million accounts registered through these pairs The pairs have been alive for 5+ years Nobody can see anything of yours through them Why not your main account Public app pairs Ways to create an extra account Creating the account Number services 01 Why not your main account This is accurate information. We know exactly where the pitfalls of these problems are. Your own app hash: 99% logged out Logging in to my.telegram.org from an account you have no access to, to get an app hash, and then any request through that app hash means a 99% chance the account is logged out. You can check it. Bans just for low trust are frequent Accounts are banned simply because Telegram does not trust them, and such bans are frequent. You can check this too. Using your own account is a really stupid idea. Copied session keys can be revoked Running an imported TData/session key in Telegram Desktop and TgWitness at the same time can trigger AUTH_KEY_DUPLICATED . Telegram invalidates that authorization, so both copies need a new login. A dedicated account does not prevent this. Fully quit the original client and keep it closed while using its imported session. For parallel use, sign in to TgWitness by phone or QR to create a separate authorization; other separately authorized clients can remain signed in. Read the session import warning Telegram documentation Logout errors: AUTH_KEY_UNREGISTERED, SESSION_REVOKED Creating your own app hash: obtaining api_id 02 Why TgWitness works through public app hash/app ID pairs That is why we built TgWitness on public app hash/app ID pairs. By our logic, bans are less likely with them: more than a million Telegram accounts have been registered through these pairs, and many different programs work through them. By our logic, this is better than working directly with a personal app hash: these pairs have been alive for 5+ years for sure. Your own new pair Created at my.telegram.org from the account. About 99% of accounts logged out One new application, one account Public pairs of the pool The same pairs many programs use. Over a million accounts registered Many different programs Working for 5+ years Why nobody can see anything of yours through these pairs The pair is a name, not a key Telegram asks for the API ID and API hash when a program connects and when it requests a login code. They identify the application and give no access to any account; Telethon's documentation notes that one pair works with any phone number. Your session key never leaves your server Signing in creates an authorization key by a Diffie–Hellman exchange between your TgWitness and Telegram; the key itself is never sent. Telegram's documentation: after authorization the key becomes associated with the user, and every call with this key runs as that user. Other programs with the same pair have their own keys and cannot use yours. Traffic is encrypted with your key Every request and answer is encrypted with the session's authorization key, not with the API hash. Knowing the API hash decrypts nothing. The owner of a pair sees nothing Telegram has no method that lists accounts, sessions or messages by API ID. The owner of a pair sees only its app settings at my.telegram.org. Only your account sees which app it is Settings → Devices of your own account lists each session's app name and API ID, device, IP address and dates. Nobody else gets this list. Telegram documentation User authorization: the key becomes the user auth.sendCode: api_id, api_hash initConnection Creating an authorization key MTProto encryption account.getAuthorizations What a session record holds Obtaining api_id Telegram apps' open source code Libraries and discussions Telethon: s

pages.title: Start in minutes

pages.text: Poke around the demo first, then connect your own account. Look around without an account Get the project, have Python 3.11 or later , run the demo. The launcher sets up everything else. git clone https://github.com/phishdestroy/TgWitness.git cd TgWitness Windows .\scripts\Demo.cmd Linux / macOS sh start.sh --demo A workspace with made-up messages opens in the browser. Open a chat, compare an edit, look at an export. No Telegram involved. A sample workspace. Your own journal starts separately. Start your own workspace Close the demo, then: Windows .\Start.cmd Linux / macOS sh start.sh Open the address the launcher shows and paste the panel access token from the file it names. That's for TgWitness, not Telegram. Capture your first message Connect a dedicated Telegram account. Pick a group or channel and start observation. Send a message in your test group and watch it appear in the journal. For a server installation, follow Keep it running .

pages.title: Connect an account
pages.description: Connect Telegram by QR code, phone number or session import. Choose sources and check that new messages reach your journal.
pages.keywords: qr phone session tdata api id hash account sources
pages.text: One workspace = one account, its journal and its key. Choose how to sign in Accounts → add a workspace → connection settings. Use a separate account for this. QR code: scan it from Telegram's Devices screen and confirm. Phone number: number, code, then 2FA password if you have one. Session import: your own session file or Telegram Desktop data. Use a built-in API profile or your own API ID and hash. It only identifies the app, it doesn't log you in or hide anything. Need a proxy first? You can choose and test the connection route before signing in. Each account has its own route. Choose what to observe Pick the chats, groups or channels you need. Check collection settings, media included. Start it and check the connection and recent activity. The account has to have access. Admins and members see different things, the journal shows what this account got. Whole account? Sources → Observation scope → Investigation mode , check it, Save scope . Full walkthrough: investigating a whole account . Check the whole path In your test group, send a message from another account, edit it, delete it. All three should show up in the journal. Then export and verify . "Connected" means the connection works. A captured test message means events actually arrive. Add another account New workspace in Accounts , same steps. Note each account's key fingerprint so you can tell exports apart later.

pages.title: Choose a proxy
pages.description: Maintain automatic MTProxy routes or use your own proxy. Choose IP modes, fallback rules and the route for external requests.
pages.keywords: mtproto mtproxy socks5 http automatic pool IP modes fallback network public lists
pages.text: Keep the account online, and decide yourself whether it may ever show your server's IP. Choose the IP mode first 01 Hide the address Proxy only. If none works, it waits. 02 Direct as a last resort Goes direct after a delay, back to a proxy once one works. 03 Server behind a tunnel or VPN Direct is fine. It doesn't set up or check the VPN for you. The route chooses the connection. The IP mode determines whether a direct connection is permitted. Let the pool maintain the route Account → Settings → Connection settings . Pick the IP mode and Automatic MTProxy , or a fixed route. Save, Test Telegram connection (works before sign-in too). Start collecting and send yourself a test message. New workspaces start on automatic MTProxy with Hide the address . The pool pulls four public lists, checks servers, keeps the good ones and swaps out dead ones. Use your own proxy SOCKS5, HTTP CONNECT, a Telegram proxy link or an operator catalog. Pause observation before switching. Fake TLS secrets ( ee …) don't work. Rotation, sharing and retry settings Parameters → Automatic MTProxy : failure thresholds, cooldowns, rotation, accounts per proxy. Limit 1 means an account waits rather than share. Different proxies can still share an exit IP. Separate Telegram from external requests MTProxy only carries Telegram. Timestamps, notifications, copies and code checks go through a separate SOCKS5/HTTP proxy, the account's SOCKS5/HTTP route, or direct if the mode allows. Or turn them off. TGWITNESS_PROXY_FEED_PROXY sets the route for list downloads. The witness has its own settings. None of this touches your browser or system network. More: modes and defaults , who may change routes .

pages.title: Export and verify
pages.description: Export captured Telegram history, verify signatures and compare a journal with a checkpoint retained by an independent witness.
pages.keywords: evidence signature hash integrity verify zip fingerprint checkpoint s3 backup restore recovery object lock
pages.text: Hand someone files they can check themselves against your workspace. Retain a reference Export signed ZIP Recipient verifies New to signatures and checkpoints? Change a sample record and see which checks catch it. Keeping a copy away from the collector? Go to S3 setup , Object Lock or verified recovery . Retain a trusted reference Write down the workspace key fingerprint somewhere other than the collector. While collecting, keep signed checkpoints elsewhere too, or run an independent witness . That's what the recipient checks the key and an earlier journal state against. Download the signed ZIP Exports → signed evidence ZIP. It has the whole journal and a signed file manifest. Shape the readable report in Report studio , or send only selected data as a handover extract . HTML, PDF and JSON reports carry their own seals. CSV is just a working copy; for integrity use the CSV inside the verified ZIP. Verify with a trusted copy of TgWitness In the project environment, with your own fingerprint and paths: python -m tgwitness.verify evidence.zip --fingerprint TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 --checkpoint retained-checkpoint.json A pass shows key_pinned: true and checkpoint_checked: true . Keep that output next to the archive. The checkpoint has to be at or before the end of the export. Use the verification result Files: the manifest binds their hashes, the signatures bind the journal. Any change shows up. Identity: the fingerprint you kept proves it's the key you expected. Earlier state: a checkpoint compares the export with a journal prefix saved before the handoff. Coverage: gaps, acquisition results and a send → edit → delete test show what this setup actually caught. Details: what verification proves and what it doesn't . Set up the S3 off-site copy Exports → Off-site copy in your workspace. Works with AWS S3 and anything S3-compatible. It copies journal segments, saved files, checkpoints with their timestamps and finished chat exports, each encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it leaves the collector. The online demo shows these controls with uploads off. Only enter real credentials in your own install. The complete panel with advanced options expanded. No storage credentials are shown. Storage settings in Exports → Off-site copy Field What to enter Endpoint Storage URL, no bucket path or credentials. Example: https://s3.example.invalid . Region Whatever your provider needs. Default us-east-1 . Bucket An existing bucket you can write to. Example: example-case-backup . Folder in the bucket Prefix, default tgwitness . A per-workspace prefix is added on top. Access key ID / Secret access key Both together, stored in the vault. Leave both empty later to keep them. Path-style addresses On: endpoint/bucket . Off: bucket.endpoint . Depends on the provider. Copy interval 1 to 1,440 minutes, default 5. Only while the app runs. Object Lock retention Days and mode, if the bucket supports Object Lock. Zero keeps the bucket default. Create the bucket, fill in destination and credentials with Keep an off-site copy unticked, hit Save off-site copy . Test connection uploads an encrypted test object. Download encryption key and keep it away from the collector. No key, no recovery. Tick Keep an off-site copy , save, then Copy now or let the schedule run. Check retention and copy progress Under More options pick retention days and GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE . TgWitness reads the retention back from an uploaded object and tells you: confirmed, missing or check failed. The panel shows the last pass, object count, bytes, copied journal boundary and errors. A missing local file is reported and retried next pass, the rest keeps copying. Uploads go over Direct, SOCKS5 or HTTP. With an MTProxy-only route the copy waits with an error. Keep the recovery key separately The key JSON has the decryption key, destination, prefix and key fingerprint. For recovery you need it plus storage credentials with read access. Changed endpoint, bucket or prefix? Download the key aga

pages.title: See how evidence works
pages.description: Follow a message from capture to checkpoint. Change a sample record, recalculate its SHA-256 chain and see what a retained checkpoint detects.
pages.keywords: visual animation diagram formula sha256 hash chain canonical signature tamper learn
pages.text: Messages change. Your record of what you saw shouldn't, and anyone should be able to check that. Two small experiments below. Fake messages, everything runs in your browser, nothing goes to Telegram. From a chat export to a verifiable record A Telegram Desktop export saves the history you can see right now as HTML or JSON. TgWitness adds a running journal of changes, signatures on every record and checkpoints others can compare against. Task Telegram Desktop export TgWitness Read saved conversations HTML or JSON with selected media Saved chats, searchable journal and offline reports Follow a change over time The history available when exported Old versions, later edits and deletions, all kept Check files after handover Standard HTML/JSON export files are unsigned Signed manifest, signed records and sealed reports, checked against a trusted key Compare with an earlier retained state Keep a separate reference copy or hash Signed checkpoints, a separate witness and optional external timestamps The comparison is based on the Telegram Desktop export code as of 2 November 2026. One message, three observations A new message, an edit and a deletion become three separate records. The edit doesn't overwrite the first one, and the deletion doesn't erase it. 01 / MESSAGE JOURNEY Illustrative sequence CURRENT CHAT VIEW Message #42 Message deleted The message has disappeared from the chat view. OBSERVATION JOURNAL 3 records 01 message.new Meet at 10:00 ✓ 02 message.edited Meet at 11:00 ✓ 03 message.deleted Deletion notice for #42 ✓ Play sequence Next event → Reset Ready / 0 of 3 All three received observations remain in the journal. Simplified path for one already selected source. Operational records also share the real journal. Capture depends on what the account can see and what Telegram delivers. Telegram doesn't say who deleted a message or exactly when. TgWitness leaves those fields empty instead of guessing. Change a record. Follow the hash. Every record contains the hash of the one before it. A checkpoint kept somewhere else pins the journal length and the last hash. 02 / HASH-CHAIN SANDBOX Real SHA-256 · sample records Original Alter record 2 Rebuild its hashes Remove the tail RECORD 01 Message received h₁ = SHA-256(e₁) Links to 64 zeroes RECORD 02 Meet at 11:00 h₂ = SHA-256(e₂) Includes h₁ RECORD 03 Deletion observed h₃ = SHA-256(e₃) Includes h₂ RETAINED ELSEWHERE 3 records · head h₃ Compare this fixed boundary with the supplied journal. Altering an event changes its hash. Rebuilding the chain changes its head. Removing the tail makes it shorter than the retained checkpoint. Inspect record 2 and the full hashes This is the exact UTF-8 JSON hashed in this example. Values are fictional; the nine fields and serialization match the journal format. Saved record 2 hash Recalculated record 2 hash This sandbox computes hashes, not signatures. The real verifier also checks every event’s Ed25519 signature, sequence and link. Rebuilding hashes alone cannot create valid signatures under the trusted key. The actual rules, in a few lines HASH + SIGNATURE h 0 = 0 64 h i = hex(SHA-256(C(e i ))) σ i = Ed25519.Sign(sk, unhex(h i )) C is the nine event fields as UTF-8 JSON: sorted keys, no extra whitespace, no ASCII escaping, no NaN/infinity. previous_hash is h i−1 , h 0 is 64 zeros, signatures cover the 32 raw digest bytes. The fields: seq , observed_at , source_at , kind , chat_id , message_id , actor_id , payload , previous_hash . Full spec: event encoding . RETAINED CHECKPOINT N export ≥ N checkpoint h export [N checkpoint ] = H checkpoint Check the checkpoint signature against the pinned key, then compare it with the journal. A later export can be longer, but it has to match at the checkpoint. Three questions, three different checks 01 / INTEGRITY Did this record change? Hashes and signatures against a key you trust. 02 / CONTINUITY What was retained earlier? Compare the export with checkpoints a witness kept. 03 / DELIVERY Did these test events

pages.title: Investigate across all chats
pages.description: Run an end-to-end Telegram investigation across channels, groups, private chats and bots: whole-account capture, history, people, links, files, timelines and verified evidence.
pages.keywords: use cases scenarios investigation all chats whole account history dossier people links files timeline case package
pages.text: A whole case across channels, groups, private chats and bots: collect, connect the dots, rebuild the timeline, hand it over. One made-up incident, start to finish. Collection, search and people profiles find the records, Case Board organizes them, Report studio presents them. WORKED CASE / A CHANGED PAYMENT DESTINATION One incident. Four conversations. A trail to reconstruct. A channel post points to a bot. A group talks about a new payment link and the bot shows it. The post gets edited, a private chat repeats the link, a group message vanishes. Who posted each version? Where did the link appear? Which file was preserved? What changed, and when? 1. All chats 2. History & files 3. Live actions 4. Connections 5. Timeline 6. Other accounts 7. Case package History loading, AI, MCP, OCR and webhooks: Work the archive . 1. Establish coverage across the whole account Whole-account scope only on a dedicated account. A main account gets chosen chats or a folder. Connect the account in its own workspace. Note the case reference, account ID, workspace and key fingerprint. Sources → Observation scope → Investigation mode : Whole account , all four source types, Own actions . Every new chat gets its profile and last 200 visible messages saved. Save scope and confirm. Load chats and compare with the account's chat list. The limit is 1,000 dialogs (up to 20,000 in Parameters → Chats read from the account's list ); chats beyond it show up once they get active. Recording settings → All visible activity , check attachment limits and disk space. Start, then test with a message, an edit and a deletion. Channels Groups Private chats Bots ONE ACCOUNT / ONE SIGNING KEY All selected account-visible activity → one journal Messages · edits · deletion notices · visible reactions · membership events · own actions "Whole account" means every chat this account can open, minus exclusions. No secret chats. New chats join as they appear; old history isn't downloaded automatically. 2. Acquire history and preserve the files Make a Case Board collection and bookmark what matters. Keep a source register: chat ID, title, account, role, start of live capture, history result, media result, gaps. Choose the acquisition that answers the question Need Action in the panel What it provides History across enabled chats Sources → Load full history Available past messages enter the workspace journal, with pause/resume and a signed progress report. History guide . Existing chat context in the journal Sources → Recording settings → History snapshot Recent messages as signed records. 500 by default, up to 10,000 in Parameters → Largest history snapshot . Complete currently visible history of one chat Full chat export → Export full chat, or Chats → Export chat A separate signed bundle with chat.json and chat.html , one per chat. Context when a new chat appears Observation scope → When a new chat or bot appears Its profile and up to 1,000 recent messages (200 in Investigation mode). Not applied to existing chats. Attachment bytes Download visible attachments + per-type limits Look for media.saved with SHA-256 and size. Queued, skipped or failed means not saved. A chat export doesn't go into the journal or people profiles. To search old history inside TgWitness, use Load full history or snapshots. Here: the channel, the group, the bot chat and the private chat, plus the invoice file and its hash. What was deleted before capture is gone. 3. Keep the evolving conversation and your own actions Keep it running. Star the hot chats as priority, tune rechecks in Recording settings → Recheck , and keep an eye on recheck.completed , FloodWait and media results. Chats → Profile → Save profile now saves the chat's description, bot commands and other metadata. Following a bot or invitation as part of the case Chats → Open Telegram link , save the preview first. Link and preview become signed records. If needed, Join / open and observe joins the chat or starts the bot with its start paramete

pages.title: Build a Case Board
pages.description: Collect saved observations, exact highlights and action slices on a private board, discuss them with your team and present a collection.
pages.keywords: case board bookmarks highlights slices collections comments presentation
pages.text: Turn saved messages into a case your team works on together. Bookmarks, exact quotes, slices and discussion, each linked to its source. Every change is a signed revision. From a message to a case card Investigation → Case Board (Standard or Expert mode). Make a collection for the case. In Journal or a chat hit To board (or B ). The card lands in Inbox, give it a title and move it. Select text in a message, Highlight → board keeps the exact quote and version. Note why it matters. Discuss, set a status, jump back to the source whenever needed. Presentation walks the team through it. Follow one changed payment link Synthetic example · local illustration Capture. Open saved observation #142 and its message version. Bookmark. Keep the quote, source reference and your question on a card. Review. Add a team comment and move the card to Review. Present. Walk through the collection and open the cited source context. Saved observation #142 “Use the new payment link.” Operations chat · message 38 · observed 09:12 UTC Card: changed destination Use the new payment link. Question: which destination appeared in the earlier version? Team review Analyst: compare with observation #101. Status: Review · revision retained Source context Card → saved version → earlier observation The annotation and the Telegram observation remain separately identifiable. Play example Pause Next step Reset example Save a useful range once Shift-click two messages for Slice between , use Slice by time , or save the current Journal filters. Show records added since bookmark shows what came in later. Time slices use observation time; message-ID slices follow those messages as they change. Give each colleague the right role Reviewer reads, Analyst adds cards and comments, Operator also manages collections and decisions. Chat permissions apply to cards too. Carry the work into a deliverable Slices export as signed JSON or CSV. Reports can include bookmarks, slices and comments, set that in Report studio . For a limited recipient, use a handover . Details: Case Board reference .

pages.title: Design a report
pages.description: Choose report data, one of eight designs and the contents, then preview and export HTML, signed PDF or a complete evidence package.
pages.keywords: report studio design contents preview PDF HTML charts transcript
pages.text: Take the reader from the case question straight to the saved records. Report studio puts together the data you pick, change histories, charts and your findings. Eight designs, HTML and native PDF. Every HTML, PDF and JSON report is sealed with your key. Build a report in three steps Exports → Configure and preview → Data : whole workspace, or pick chats, authors, dates (UTC, when TgWitness saw the record) and record types. Design & contents : pick a design and what goes in: charts, participants, transcript, changes, Case Board items, your case details and notes. Preview : check counts, activity, samples and missing ID ranges. Save, then download the format you need. Arrange the same saved material for a reader Synthetic example · schematic layout, not a generated report Select. Choose two chats and the observation period for the case. Compose. Choose a layout and the sections that answer the question. Preview. Review the selected counts and the saved before-and-after text. Verify. Generate the final file and check its signature against the trusted workspace fingerprint. Diagram layout Classic Reading series Diagram contents Message context Saved changes Selected observations 2 chats · 1 observation day Messages, edits and deletion notices Report structure Changed payment destination Case question → scope → findings → record references Message context Observation #142: “Use the new payment link.” Saved changes Before: old.example.invalid → After: new.example.invalid Review the selection 18 observations · 2 saved edits Sent, edited and observed times have separate labels. Final deliverable Signed PDF + signed JSON, or a signed ZIP with its readable report Recipient checks the file and trusted fingerprint. Play example Pause Next step Reset example Choose a reading style Classic, Editorial, Briefing, Analytics, Technical, Overview, Reading series, and Ledger & margin : same records, different look. Switching keeps your selection and notes. Any of the 25 languages. PDFs are built with bundled fonts, no browser needed. Chinese, Japanese and Korean need a font like Noto Sans CJK on the server (system-wide or in TGWITNESS_FONT_DIR ), otherwise you get HTML and JSON only. Read a change with its context Edits show before and after, deletions show the last saved version. Replies, forwards, reactions, buttons and attachments keep their references. The design preview uses the first 50,000 records, the data preview counts everything exactly. For final page layout, generate the PDF. Choose the recipient's copy deliberately Filters only shape the report, the evidence ZIP still has the full journal and files. If the recipient should get less, use a minimized handover . More: report contents , verifying the export .

pages.title: Prepare a sharing copy
pages.description: Choose the records and fields a recipient can receive, inspect the finished copy and verify its signed manifest and source journal boundary.
pages.keywords: sharing copy minimized handover disclosure redaction privacy recipient verification
pages.text: Share only what's needed, the original stays untouched. A handover is a separate signed extract: pick chats and people, hide identities or text, choose files and team notes. The manifest records what was kept, trimmed and left out. Prepare the recipient's extract Exports → Handover extract : write the purpose, pick chats and a period, Load people of the chosen chats if you need named people. Everyone else: pseudonyms, left out, or as recorded. Text and files are separate switches; phones and emails can be masked. Case Board: nothing, bookmarks and slices, or cards with comments. Team names can be swapped for aliases. Download handover extract , open it, verify it, look through it before sending. One original, a deliberate sharing copy Synthetic example · identity illustration only Select. Include the case chat and identify the person the extract is about. Minimize. Choose how another participant appears in the sharing copy. Inspect. Open the generated archive's report and records before sending it. Share. Deliver the checked copy and communicate its trusted fingerprint separately. Another participant in this example Show as recorded Use a pseudonym Leave the message out Original observation Nora · user 71002 “I received the revised link.” The source journal keeps this saved observation. Handy when several accounts work the same case. Open the group overview Open the group in Accounts . Each account shows its state, route, latency and last saved message. pages.title: Keep it secure
pages.description: See where sessions, keys and evidence live, what leaves your machine, what the protections cover and how to harden an installation.
pages.keywords: security threat model secrets vault token encryption hardening privacy vulnerability report
pages.text: What leaves your machine, what each secret opens, and what the protections cover versus what's on you. 127.0.0.1 panel address by default 256-bit random panel token 0 CDNs, analytics or remote fonts Ed25519 signature on every record Where everything lives The collector, the panel and every record stay on your machine. By default only Telegram is contacted; everything else is a separate switch. 06 / WHAT LEAVES THE MACHINE Your installation Off-site copy Notifications Timestamps Witness YOUR COMPUTER OR SERVER Panel 127.0.0.1:8787 · bearer token Collector one Telegram client per workspace DATA DIRECTORY Journal SQLite · hash-chained · signed Media files named by SHA-256 Vault Fernet · session, API pair, signing key, proxy Telegram Always · through your route The account's MTProto connection: direct, SOCKS5, HTTP or MTProxy. Hide IP mode waits for a working proxy. Direct fallback requires a mode that explicitly permits it. Off-site copy Optional · off by default Journal, files and checkpoints encrypted with AES-GCM before upload to S3-compatible storage. The key stays with you; attachments are named by keyed hashes, not their content hash. Notifications Optional · off by default Problems and change counts with chat titles. Message excerpts are sent only if you turn them on. Timestamp authority Optional · off by default Only the SHA-256 of a signed checkpoint and a random nonce. No messages, no chat names. Witness Optional · off by default Pulls signed checkpoints and capture counters with a read-only token. It cannot read conversations or change settings. Default: only the Telegram connection leaves this machine. Optional destinations are configured per workspace. Message text and media are stored unencrypted in the data directory: protect it with disk encryption and file permissions. What each secret unlocks Secret Where it is kept What it unlocks If it leaks Panel token panel-token.txt in the data directory; the browser keeps it per tab Everything in every workspace Stop TgWitness, delete panel-token.txt , start again: you get a new one Telegram session Vault, encrypted ( credentials.enc ) The Telegram account itself End the session in Telegram under Settings → Devices Signing key Vault, encrypted ( signing.enc ) Signing records under your fingerprint Checkpoints kept elsewhere, a witness and timestamps still show what existed before Vault key vault.key next to the data, or an external master key The vault Assume the session and signing key leaked too Witness token On the witness host Read-only: checkpoints and health Delete it on the Witness page, make a new one Off-site copy key Vault; download it once for recovery The off-site copy Anyone who also has the bucket can decrypt it: treat the copy as exposed What the protections cover ✓ Covered A changed, removed or reordered record: the hash chain or a signature breaks. A journal cut back or rebuilt after you saved a checkpoint elsewhere: the checkpoint stops matching. Guessing the token: 256 random bits, constant-time compare, 15 failures a minute and the address is blocked. Hostile chat content: text stays text, never HTML; attachments download as files; the panel loads nothing from other sites. A stolen data directory with an external vault key: sessions and keys stay encrypted. ! Left to you The main token can do everything. Give others scoped access and keep the main one to yourself. Whoever is admin on the machine can read everything and re-sign the journal. Keep the fingerprint and checkpoints elsewhere. Messages and media aren't encrypted by TgWitness. Encrypt the disk, lock down permissions. Plain HTTP outside localhost leaks the token. Use HTTPS or an SSH tunnel. Signatures don't tell you what was missed. Check coverage and test delivery on your own accounts and sources. Share access to a case with permissions, expiry and session limits. Harden an installation 0 of 8 done Use a dedicated Telegram account , never your main one. Keep the panel on 127.0.0.1. Remote acces

pages.description: Give reviewers and analysts access to selected accounts and chats, with separate permissions, session limits and revocable tokens.

pages.text: Share the case someone needs. Keep control of the rest. 01 Choose the evidence Whole workspaces or single chats. 02 Choose the actions View, export, or just the operations they need. 03 Set the limits A personal token with expiry, session limits and IP rules if you want. Collection scope decides what is recorded. Access scope decides what a person can see and do. Give someone access As admin, open Access . Name it, pick workspaces and chats. A reviewer needs only View . Add Export for downloads. Set limits, then press Create access . Copy the token (shown once) and send it privately with the panel address. Check what they'll see in a separate browser session first. Start with the job they need to do Person Access Result Reviewer Selected chats; view only Reads the chat, can't change anything. Analyst Selected chats; view and export Reads and downloads what the case needs. Operator Selected whole workspaces; sources and collection Decides what's observed, starts and stops collectors. These are just examples, not fixed roles. Chat-limited access never gets account settings or full journal exports. All-workspace access includes accounts added later. Change your mind at any time Edit access any time, it applies from the next request. End one session or revoke everything. Already downloaded files are gone for good. Collection keeps running. Session and IP limits Limit parallel sessions and sign-ins, set an end date, allow IPs or subnets, or lock to the first sign-in IP. Expiry counts inactivity, an open panel counts as active. Behind a proxy, check which client IP the app sees. The main key and the activity log The main token stays with the admin. Issued access can't manage other people's access or open the admin console. Access changes and sessions are signed into the journal, without tokens. The server admin can still see everything. All seven permissions and session rules: access reference .

pages.title: Set up a witness bot
pages.description: Publish signed journal checkpoints to your Telegram channel with a separate witness, its own key and read-only collector access.
pages.keywords: bot botfather telegram channel continuity checkpoint independent witness
pages.text: A separate process checks your journal and posts signed checkpoints to a channel. Two hosts, two signing keys HOST A / COLLECTOR Account + journal Telegram session Collector signing key Read-only checkpoint endpoint ← request signed answer → HOST B / WITNESS Verify + retain Pinned collector fingerprint Separate witness signing key Own journal + bot token Witness → Telegram Bot API → Your channel · signed TGW1 posts The witness pulls checks itself. Collector access is read-only. Bot publication uses the witness’s connection and token; no account session is given to the witness. 03 / CHECKPOINT DECISIONS Illustrative answers Journal grows Count goes back Same count, new head No response LAST ACCEPTED 120 records head 9c7d… → NEXT ANSWER 128 records head a4f2… Accepted: the count grows, the signature verifies and the key matches. The witness retains this new boundary. All answering examples assume a valid signature and the pinned key. Hashes here are abbreviated illustrations. A larger count alone cannot prove that the entire old prefix is unchanged; compare an export with retained checkpoints. Prepare a bot and a channel Make a bot with BotFather and let it post in your channel. Run the witness somewhere else: another host, ideally run by someone else, is worth much more than a second process next to the collector. Three steps in Extras Read-only access. Extras → Independent witness , create a token, save the file. It reads checkpoints and health, nothing else. Channel and interval. Telegram channel or Discord webhook, plus a collector address the witness can reach. Save the settings file. Launch. Put witness.json , witness-token.txt and bot-token.txt together on the witness host and run: python -m tgwitness.witness run --config witness.json --check-config python -m tgwitness.witness run --config witness.json Wait for the first signed post in the channel, then save the witness fingerprint somewhere safe. Discord instead? Save the webhook URL as discord-webhook.txt . One witness posts to one place; long checks arrive as a file on Discord. Choose how often to publish Posting every check gives a steady outside record: every five minutes is about 288 posts a day per workspace. Advanced settings can post only on changes or problems, use a proxy or a custom Bot API. What does the bot actually attest to? It asks the collector for a signed checkpoint, checks it against the expected key and keeps its own signed journal, including missed and rejected answers. It checks the journal state, it doesn't watch Telegram itself. For that, run a controlled delivery test. Check the evidence later Keep the witness journal, the posts and the fingerprints. How to check them against the collector's export.

pages.title: Keep it running
pages.description: Run TgWitness on a server with persistent storage, private panel access, backups and checks after a restart.

pages.text: Keep the collector up and the data safe through restarts. Choose a launch method Native: the launcher plus service templates in deploy/ . Docker, from the project folder: docker compose up -d --build --wait docker compose exec tgwitness cat /data/panel-token.txt The panel listens on localhost:8787. Open it locally or through an SSH tunnel, with the token from the second command. Keep the whole data directory Native: data/live . Docker: the tgwitness-data volume. Journals, sessions and keys belong together. A signed export is evidence, not a backup. Stop collecting first. Copy the whole data directory somewhere safe, off the host. Try restoring it on a separate install before you trust it. Check after a restart Check the workspace and key, the connection, sources and that new messages come in. TgWitness catches up what Telegram still has, not everything that happened while it was down. "Healthy" container means the web server answers. Whether collection works, a test message and the witness will tell. Publish only what you intend HTTPS, volumes, updates and restore are in the deployment reference. What's actually been tested: validation record .

pages.title: Find what went wrong
pages.description: Check panel access, Telegram connection, missing messages, FloodWait and witness status using the right signals for each problem.
pages.keywords: help error token login disconnected floodwait gap pts qts recovery github
pages.text: Start from the symptom, check one thing at a time. The panel asks for a token It wants the panel token from the file the launcher printed. Docker: docker compose exec tgwitness cat /data/panel-token.txt . Not a Telegram code, not a bot token, not the witness token. Telegram does not connect Run the connection check. On a public proxy, pick another one and save. Check the proxy type and secret format. Refreshing lists doesn't switch the route by itself. Connected, but no new messages Is observation running, in the right workspace? Is the source selected and visible to that account? Send a unique message in your test group and search for it. Look for interruptions or Telegram errors in the journal. A quiet chat just has nothing new. If completeness matters, run a controlled delivery test. FloodWait or a gap after a restart FloodWait is Telegram saying "slow down". Wait it out and lighten the load, reconnecting won't help. After a restart TgWitness catches up what Telegram still has; the rest is a gap, so write it down. The bot is configured but posts nothing Is the witness running, can the bot post in the channel, can it reach the collector and Bot API? Look in its journal for failed posts. A poll on the collector side doesn't mean a post went out. Where is GitHub token integration? Planned. Extras describes the proposed fork and build verification workflow. There is currently no GitHub token form or automated attestation that a running installation matches a repository. See the current feature status . Reporting a bug? Version, OS, steps and a redacted error. Never put sessions, tokens, private messages or the data directory in a public issue.

pages.description: Load past messages from enabled sources, pause and resume, and verify a signed progress report.

pages.text: In Sources , review the enabled chats, pause observation, choose Standard API or Takeout export, then choose Load full history . The run fixes that list of sources and reads their available past messages into Chats and the signed observation journal. Media uses the existing attachment settings and durable download queue. This is separate from the per-chat signed JSON/HTML export. For account-wide collection, select Whole account , start observation to load its source list, and review that list before starting history. The dialog-list limit still applies (1,000 by default, adjustable in Parameters). A successful run does not prove that every account dialog was listed. Chats discovered or enabled later need another run. Pause observation before starting history; one acquisition owns an account at a time. Choose one to five attachment workers and whether to preserve available Recent Actions and compare previously saved versions. Takeout may require approval in Telegram and a server-specified wait. These options remain fixed on resume. See Backfill behavior and evidence contract for transport, retry and trust details. Pause, restart and partial results # Pause history stops reading. Continue history resumes from the last committed message in each source; restarting the app also leaves the run paused until resumed. Resuming requires the same idle Telegram account. The message observation, attachment job and cursor commit in one transaction. A resumed run does not repeat its already committed observations. Live capture or a separate, explicitly started run may independently observe the same message. Each source (each Telegram split range in Takeout) fixes an upper message ID on its first read. Newer messages belong to live observation, not to that source's remaining historical pages. Inaccessible sources and sources disabled during acquisition remain visible as failed or skipped. Other sources continue; the overall result is incomplete. FloodWait delays respect the saved account backoff. Transient failures retry up to five times; exhaustion and low disk space pause with the cursor intact. End this history run preserves saved observations. It does not remove them or cancel standard-API attachment jobs. Ending Takeout marks its remaining Takeout files as skipped; pausing keeps them resumable. A new run reads enabled sources anew. History completion describes history reads only. Attachments may remain pending, fail, or be excluded by the configured policy. Check media receipts in the journal and the attachment queue; only a completed receipt with preserved bytes constitutes a saved attachment. The history operation is an explicit snapshot request and is separate from switches that select categories of future live events. Transfer and verify # Save the signed progress report , then use Export evidence to download the journal and saved attachments. A later evidence export may include additional records; the report binds its counters to the journal prefix at the time it was created. Run the verifier from a trusted checkout of this version: python tgwitness/verify.py tgwitness-history-report.json --evidence evidence.zip --fingerprint TRUSTED_FINGERPRINT Keep the expected signing-key fingerprint independently. The verifier checks the report signature, the evidence archive, the report checkpoint, source plan, account and counts of saved/unavailable messages. New runs also bind source progress and options to signed cursor events. Without --evidence , it checks only the signed report and its internal consistency. Legacy progress fields and attachment summaries remain signed collector statements. The evidence verifier checks archived media bytes. Neither signing nor finishing the available history proves Telegram origin, an atomic snapshot, or historical completeness. Messages can change while reading; deleted messages and intermediate edits outside available Recent Actions, and Secret Chats, are not recovered. An operator controlling the signi

pages.description: Search saved messages, review AI inputs and keep analytical reports with their source references.

pages.text: Workflow guide · Wiki Use Journal for local search without AI; full-text search (preview) matches word forms, phrases, domains and @usernames. For Ask the archive , first enable and configure a provider in Integrations . The workspace selector chooses the account; the form chooses chats and the observation period. Retrieval runs locally. An exact phrase or domain narrows retrieval; a message ID requests saved versions. Review the excerpts and open their journal records or context. There is no vector database or automatic Telegram action. Providers and consent # AI starts disabled in every workspace. Only the main administrator can configure the model, endpoint, encrypted API key, context/output limits, timeout and daily request budget. The key is never returned to the browser. Keep a blank key field to retain the current key, or explicitly remove it. Ollama uses its documented /api/chat endpoint with non-streaming JSON output. Its default address is http://127.0.0.1:11434 on the TgWitness server. The operator can change it using TGWITNESS_AI_LOCAL_ENDPOINT ; this is not a model-controlled address. Install the selected model yourself. TgWitness does not download it automatically. The compatible provider expects a base URL ending in /v1 and the Chat Completions protocol : messages , JSON response mode, max_completion_tokens , and choices[0].message.content . Services lacking these fields are not supported. Connection testing sends synthetic text and counts toward the request budget. Every request uses the workspace's configured outside route. A blocked route or Telegram-only MTProxy is an error; there is no direct retry. A deliberately configured local Ollama address permits a private destination. A loopback AI endpoint requires the workspace's Direct outside route; proxy routes are rejected before transmission. For other private services the existing server-level private destination opt-in applies. The preview shows the endpoint and outside route, including the proxy host when applicable. Changing that route requires a new preview. Before generation, Data sent to the model shows the request: question, checked excerpts, event kinds, observation times and coverage markers. Telegram sessions, raw fields, provider keys, attachment bytes and the full journal are not part of that context. Uncheck unwanted sources, then explicitly approve processing. External providers may retain submitted content under their own policies. Local execution means the endpoint is local; it is not a guarantee about an independently configured service's behavior. There are at most two concurrent provider requests globally and one per workspace. A preview expires after ten minutes and can generate one answer. The provider's reported token counts are shown; a cost estimate appears only when both input and output tariffs have been configured. Failed attempts also consume the daily request budget. No automatic retries spend additional budget. Sources and limits # Retrieval uses the full-text index when it is complete: the best matches across the selected chats, with word forms. Questions about recent changes or one message's versions, and searches while the index is building, use a bounded lexical search of the newest records. The preview names the method. Retrieval returns up to 24 sources; long texts are cut around their match. Truncated excerpts and incomplete result sets are marked. The period refers to observation time , not a claim that Telegram history is complete. Workspace-wide coverage events are withheld from chat-scoped access. Missing data is described as not found in the available archive. The model receives no tools. Its source IDs are resolved against the selected records, hashes are rechecked, and quoted strings must occur in those records. Unknown IDs, changed quotes and uncited claims reject the answer. The application creates links; model-generated URLs are not used as citations. These checks establish source existence and quote accuracy, n

pages.title: Reference · Command line
pages.description: Search, read context, count activity and export saved messages from scripts and agents, with --json output, stable exit codes and scoped read-only tokens.
pages.keywords: command line cli terminal script agent json jsonl export statistics activity token skill
pages.text: Read-only MCP · Full-text search · Wiki Preview. tgwitness search , context , messages , stats and export read saved observations for scripts and AI agents. They cannot send anything to Telegram, change settings or modify the signed journal. With --json , stdout carries exactly one JSON document ( export writes JSON Lines). Progress, hints and errors go to stderr. Exit codes are stable: Code Meaning 0 Success, including an empty result 1 Failure: unreachable panel, unreadable data, interrupted export 2 Usage error or invalid request: bad date, unknown option, search index off 3 Unavailable now: the workspace is open in a running panel, or the panel asks to retry later (rate limit, timeout) 4 Access refused: missing, expired or revoked token, a chat outside its scope, a tool it does not allow Two ways to read # Through the panel ( --url ). The command uses the same scoped archive API as MCP. Create a connection in Integrations → MCP : choose workspaces and chats, tools and an expiry, then copy the token once. The connection is read-only, limited to those chats, rate-limited to 60 requests per minute and can be revoked or rotated at any time. Panel login tokens and Telegram credentials do not work here. export TGWITNESS_URL=https://panel.example.org # default http://127.0.0.1:8787 export TGWITNESS_MCP_TOKEN=tgw_mcp_... # or --token-file path tgwitness search 'перевод карта' --json A remote panel needs HTTPS; plain HTTP is accepted only for 127.0.0.1 , localhost and ::1 . Proxy environment variables are ignored and redirects are refused, so the token reaches only the address you give. Directly from a stopped workspace ( --data-dir ). Reads the data directory with full local access, without a token. Use it on a copy of a data directory or while collection is stopped. Signed records are never changed; like the panel, opening a workspace may bring its derived indexes up to date. When the panel has the workspace open, the command exits with code 3 ; read through the panel instead. Without --data-dir , TGWITNESS_DATA , ./data/live or the data directory of the installation running the command is used. --workspace ID selects a workspace (default default ). tgwitness messages --workspaces lists the ones you can read. Commands # Command Result tgwitness search QUERY [--chat ID] [--since] [--until] [--any] [--limit N] [--offset N] Best matches first, with word forms, exact phrases in quotes, domains and @username ( syntax ) tgwitness search QUERY --exact [--before SEQ] Exact text, newest first, without the index tgwitness context CHAT_ID MESSAGE_ID Saved messages within ten message IDs on either side tgwitness messages Chats you can read tgwitness messages CHAT_ID [--since] [--until] [--before SEQ] Saved messages of the chat, newest first tgwitness messages CHAT_ID --message ID Every saved version and deletion record of one message tgwitness stats [--chat ID] [--sender ID] [--since] [--until] [--top N] Activity statistics, below tgwitness export [--chat ID] [--since] [--until] [--output FILE] Saved observations as JSON Lines in journal order Dates are 2026-10-01 (UTC midnight) or ISO times with a timezone, 2026-10-01T09:00+03:00 . For search , messages and export they select observation time. Pages hold up to 50 records: follow next_offset ( --offset ) for ranked search and next_before ( --before ) elsewhere. Ranked search stops at 1，000 results．The final page may be shorter than --limit ；narrow the query，chat or period when more matching observations exist． Every message result carries untrusted_content: true , the workspace, chat and message IDs, the journal sequence, the saved record hash and a panel link. Edits, deletion notices and missing_on_recheck are separate records. Absence of a record does not prove that an event never happened. pages.description: Find saved messages by word forms, exact phrases, domains and @usernames, best matches first, with the index bound to the signed journal.

pages.text: Archive analysis · Local OCR and transcription · Wiki Preview. In Journal , choose Best match · word forms next to the search field. Results are ranked with BM25 and match other forms of the same word: перевод finds переводом and переводы , transfer finds transfers , a Chinese phrase is found without spaces. Newest first · exact text keeps the previous substring search over the whole record. The index is derived data. It is rebuilt from the signed journal, is never signed itself and never enters an export. The original records do not change. Search syntax # Write Finds перевод карта Records containing both words, in any form "переводом на карту" The exact phrase, in this order бонус OR подарок Either word перевод -казино Records without the excluded word example.com The domain and its subdomains, also in hidden links and button URLs @username , t.me/username Mentions and links of the account, and messages it sent #tag The hashtag +79991234567 , a wallet address, an e-mail address The same value in text or links from:@username , from:123456 Messages from that sender chat:-1001234567890 One chat; it can only narrow your own access id:42 Saved versions of message 42 since:2026-01-01 until:2026-01-31 Observation period; a date without a time covers the whole day kind:edited Only edits ( new , snapshot , edited , recovered ) source:ocr , source:transcription , source:all Recognized text instead of, or with, messages Prepositions and other function words are ignored when other words are present. Look-alike letters mixed into a word (a Latin a inside a Cyrillic word), fullwidth and decorative Unicode letters and invisible characters are normalized. Languages # The language is detected per record from its script and letters: Script Matching Cyrillic Russian and Ukrainian lemmas with pymorphy3 . Without the optional Ukrainian dictionary a light Ukrainian stemmer is used Latin English Snowball stemmer; diacritics are ignored Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar Overlapping character pairs: any phrase is found without spaces. Chinese queries are split into words with jieba Other scripts Exact words The Ukrainian dictionary ( pymorphy3-dicts-uk ) is distributed under GPL-3.0, so it is not installed by default. Install it with pip install "tgwitness[uk-dictionary]" ; the index notices the new analyzer and rebuilds itself. Where the index lives # Mode Storage Use On disk (default) search/fulltext.sqlite3 in the workspace directory Large archives; survives restarts In memory only Nothing on disk; rebuilt at every start No derived copy of message text on disk Off No index; Newest first · exact text remains Minimal installations The main administrator chooses the mode under Journal → Filters → Search index for each workspace. TGWITNESS_FULLTEXT=disk|memory|off sets the default for workspaces without their own choice. Switching to memory or off deletes the file. The index file has the same protection as the journal: it sits in the private data directory. It is not encrypted, and is not part of backups or off-site copies. New records are indexed in the background within seconds; a search also indexes a short backlog first, so a record saved a moment ago is found. An existing journal is indexed after the update without blocking the panel; until then, results cover the indexed records and the journal shows the progress. Rebuild index starts again from the first record. python -m tgwitness index status --data-dir data/live python -m tgwitness index rebuild --data-dir data/live --json rebuild needs the panel to be stopped (exit code 3 otherwise). With --json , standard output carries only the result; progress goes to standard error. Results and the signed journal # The index stores the sequence number and hash of the last journal record it covers and checks them against the journal when it opens. A replaced, restored or edited journal causes a rebuild. Every response reports this position, and every hit is read back from the signed j

pages.title: Reference · Read-only MCP
pages.description: Connect an MCP client to selected workspaces and chats with expiring, revocable access.
pages.keywords: MCP integrations stdio Streamable HTTP VS Code token scope
pages.text: Connect an analyst client to selected workspaces and chats. TgWitness serves Streamable HTTP at /mcp in the panel process . Each connection has its own token, expiry and permitted tools. MCP cannot send Telegram messages, change settings or modify the signed journal. The same connections work with the command line . Workflow guide · Wiki Install and check # Use the Python environment that runs the panel. From a source checkout: # Windows PowerShell & .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -c deploy/constraints-mcp.txt -e '.[mcp]' & .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe start.py --check # Linux / macOS .venv/bin/python -m pip install -c deploy/constraints-mcp.txt -e '.[mcp]' .venv/bin/python start.py --check Restart the panel with its usual data directory and launch arguments after installation. Readiness should include [PASS] mcp: streamable-http available . Integrations → MCP shows the runtime status and an installation command using that server's actual Python executable. Re-check refreshes this status without reloading the page; it does not install packages or restart the server. The MCP extra uses the official MCP Python SDK . deploy/constraints-mcp.txt pins the tested SDK and dependencies. Issue a connection # Enter a label and choose the workspaces and chats the client may read. Select tools individually or use a preset. Only implemented tools are offered. Choose 1, 7, 30 or 90 days, or a custom expiry between one minute and 90 days. Press Create connection . The token appears once beside the client config. Copy the token and config, then run Check connection . It initializes MCP and lists permitted tools; no messages are read . The result shows protocol version, tool names, count and elapsed time. Press Done when the credential is saved. Polling preserves the form and the shown-once card. Locking the panel clears displayed secrets. The list shows recent use, last tool, address and requests in the last minute. Revoke ends access. Rotate token revokes the old credential and issues a replacement with the same scope, tools and expiry; copy the replacement once. Panel login tokens and Telegram credentials do not work as MCP tokens. Connect your client # Select the client in the panel and copy its generated configuration. Configs use secret references or explicit placeholders; the token is copied separately. Client Configuration Connection Claude Code .mcp.json HTTP, type: "http" , bearer header Claude Desktop claude_desktop_config.json Local stdio bridge Cursor .cursor/mcp.json HTTP with an environment-variable header VS Code Local .vscode/mcp.json HTTP with a password promptString input Windsurf mcp_config.json HTTP with a bearer-header placeholder Other clients URL and Authorization header Streamable HTTP TgWitness uses bearer tokens, without OAuth discovery. Use the local stdio bridge for clients whose remote connector requires OAuth. For VS Code, input variables apply to the Local harness and are not forwarded to Copilot sessions. Configuration references: Claude Code , Cursor , VS Code . The canonical entry point for a local bridge is: python -m tgwitness.mcp_server --url https://your-panel.example/mcp Use the client's local Python with the MCP extra installed. Set TGWITNESS_MCP_TOKEN in its protected environment. Keep credentials out of command arguments and URLs. tgwitness-mcp is the same entry point. The old tgwitness.mcp_bridge module and TGWITNESS_ARCHIVE_TOKEN name remain compatibility paths with a warning; new configs use mcp_server and TGWITNESS_MCP_TOKEN . Cloudflare Tunnel # Forward the panel's /mcp route and preserve the bearer header. Opening MCP settings as an administrator registers the panel's current origin for this run. For a stable address available immediately after restart, configure TGWITNESS_PUBLIC_URL with the panel's HTTPS origin before starting the panel. Arbitrary Host and forwarded headers do not register a trusted address. Host and Origin checks reject unrelated browser origins. Responses use Cache-C

pages.title: Reference · Local OCR and transcription
pages.description: Recognize captured images and audio with a local worker; keep derived text linked to its source file.
pages.keywords: OCR transcription Tesseract Whisper Docker media attachment
pages.text: Workflow guide · Wiki Open a media.saved journal record, choose Recognize attachment , then select OCR or transcription under Ask the archive . Processing is manual and local. There is no cloud media mode or automatic upload. Original attachment bytes and media_sha256 remain unchanged; recognized text is explicitly marked as machine recognition and stored separately with the source hash, engine/model version, language, parameters and completion time. Transcripts retain returned timestamps. Search these results using Search recognized text and the OCR/transcript filter, or choose recognized text as the source of a Journal best-match search. Both match word forms through an in-memory index . This is a separate derived-data search; it does not silently turn machine recognition into original Telegram text or add it to signed events. Set up the optional worker # Version 1 requires a Linux host with a local Docker daemon. Windows installations can run TgWitness inside a Linux VM/WSL environment with its own local daemon. The panel never decodes an untrusted attachment itself. docker build -f deploy/media-worker/Dockerfile -t tgwitness-media:local . export TGWITNESS_MEDIA_IMAGE=tgwitness-media:local Set these variables in the TgWitness service environment and restart it. The daemon socket defaults to /var/run/docker.sock ; rootless deployments can set TGWITNESS_DOCKER_SOCKET . The worker explicitly uses that Unix socket rather than a remote Docker context. Do not expose a Docker API to panel users or mount its socket inside the recognition container. For transcription, separately install a CTranslate2-compatible Whisper model, then set TGWITNESS_WHISPER_MODEL_DIR to its directory. The worker loads it with local_files_only=True ; the selected model and input are mounted read-only. See the engine's model-loading documentation . The supplied OCR image includes English and Russian trained data. Build another language into your image when needed; language codes follow Tesseract's CLI . No model is fetched while processing. Build/download setup may use the network; each actual recognition container has networking disabled. Install the image before enabling it; runtime uses --pull=never . Bounds and recovery # The container runs as an unprivileged user with a read-only root, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges , one CPU, 2 GiB memory, a PID limit and a bounded temporary filesystem. Only a verified copy of the selected file and an optional model directory are mounted. The collector's database, vault and session are not mounted. The Docker runtime flags enforce these limits; this remains a container boundary, not a hardware enclave. Files are limited to 50 MiB, images to 20 million pixels, audio to 30 minutes with a known duration, and processing to five minutes. One worker runs at a time, with at most 20 queued/running jobs and 100 retained jobs per workspace. Cancel stops the container; retry creates a new job linked to the prior attempt. Interrupted jobs are marked after restart. Processing can fail when a model cannot fit the configured limits; it does not silently run without isolation.

pages.title: Reference · Outgoing webhooks
pages.description: Send scoped events to HTTPS receivers with HMAC signatures, retries and delivery status.
pages.keywords: webhooks HMAC n8n SIEM integrations notifications retries
pages.text: Workflow guide · Wiki Open Integrations → Outgoing webhooks in the selected workspace. Add an HTTPS receiver, choose collector/media/export events, and optionally select chats for new observations and changes. Message text is off by default. Enabling excerpts adds at most 1,000 characters to message-change events; raw Telegram fields and credentials are never sent. Copy the HMAC secret once into the receiver's protected configuration. It is encrypted in TgWitness's vault and cannot be retrieved from the panel. Remove and recreate a destination to rotate it. Send synthetic test queues a test with no chat content; refresh delivery status to see its outcome. Delivery extends the existing notification loop alongside Apprise. It uses the workspace's outside route and existing private-destination restrictions. There is no direct fallback or redirect following. URLs must not contain credentials, query strings or fragments; private addresses require the server-level network opt-in, not a setting a panel user can bypass. Payload and signature # Schema: tgwitness.webhook/1 . Every payload contains event_id , timestamp , workspace , type , synthetic , and counters. Journal-based events include their sequence and hash. Full-export completion and synthetic tests are delivery events, with no invented signed journal reference. Telegram deletion notices and missing_on_recheck remain distinct types. The X-TgWitness-Signature header is t=UNIX_SECONDS,v1=HEX_HMAC_SHA256 . Compute HMAC over the exact bytes timestamp + "." + raw_request_body , using the displayed secret as UTF-8 bytes. Compare signatures in constant time before parsing or acting on the body. Reject timestamps more than five minutes from your clock. The timestamp is refreshed on each delivery attempt. Use event_id as an idempotency key in durable storage, with an atomic unique constraint before side effects. A valid signature alone does not prevent a recent request from being replayed. Keep processed IDs for at least the entire retry window; retain them longer if the receiver can reprocess stored events. Retries # Deliveries are queued durably before HTTP requests. They use at-least-once semantics: a lost acknowledgement or restart may deliver an event again with the same ID. There are eight attempts with exponential backoff, starting at 15 seconds and capped at one hour. Success requires a 2xx response. Exhausted jobs leave a visible error; delivery is not guaranteed after retries end. The queue holds 1,000 deliveries. When full, scanning journal events pauses and resumes after space is available. A full-export completion that cannot be queued sets a visible queue error. Up to five deliveries are attempted per notification pass, and the latest 100 attempt records are retained. Removing a destination also removes its pending deliveries. n8n example # Import the example workflow . It is inactive and contains no secrets or downstream actions. Set TGWITNESS_WEBHOOK_SECRET in the n8n worker environment, allow that environment access, and allow the crypto builtin for the Code node. The example uses the Webhook node's raw-body option, checks signature/freshness, and acknowledges validated events. This matches the node's documented implementation . Before adding SIEM writes or notifications, add durable idempotency storage keyed by event_id . Restrict n8n workflow editing and execution-log retention according to the data you elected to send. TgWitness adds no inbound commands.

Use the panel token for your installation method to open the panel. If you need a proxy, save it under Account → Settings → Connection settings → Change connection route . In Account , enter your phone number and press Continue , choose QR code → Show QR code , or select files and press Connect account .
