pages.title: Reference · Accounts and session formats
pages.description: Sign in by phone, QR code or auth key, import Telethon, Pyrogram or Telegram Desktop sessions, and run several accounts.
pages.keywords: login phone qr session tdata pyrogram telethon import api pair
pages.text: TgWitness signs in as a Telegram user account (not a bot) over MTProto, using Telethon. Each account lives in its own workspace (called a workspace in the API and command-line tools) with its own session, sources, journal and signing key. Session files, session strings and Auth Keys are account authorizations : whoever holds one can act as that account. They do not contain message history. [!WARNING] Do not use anything you cannot afford to lose. We strongly advise against connecting personal or otherwise valuable accounts, and against creating an API ID / API hash on an account you value. This is not about TgWitness being untested: Telegram restricts and permanently bans accounts unpredictably — for request volumes it happens to consider excessive, regardless of the client or purpose, with no adequate documentation. Many bans are irreversible. Use dedicated accounts. Smooth test runs depend on Telegram, not on the software, and guarantee nothing for later. At a glance Before you start: API ID and API hash Phone number · QR code · Auth Key + DC ID Account files : Telethon .session · Pyrogram .session · Session + JSON pair · TData · StringSession · Account JSON Identify what you have · Unsupported formats Multiple accounts · Keeping account files safe · Troubleshooting At a glance # What you have Tab in Add account You will also need The phone number and access to its login codes Phone 2FA password if enabled Telegram open on another device QR code 2FA password if enabled A .session file (Telethon or Pyrogram) Files Optional companion JSON for app settings .session + .json with the same name Files (select both) Usually nothing else A Telegram Desktop tdata folder Files (as a ZIP) The Desktop local passcode if one is set A Telethon StringSession (text, .txt , .tgwitness-session ) Files No separate API pair required A .json with a session or Auth Key Files No separate API pair required An Auth Key (512 hex characters) and its DC number Auth key Optional User ID TgWitness recognises files by their contents , not their names. Renaming a file never converts it. Before you start: API ID and API hash # You can sign in without creating a Telegram API application. When no pair is entered, imported or already saved in the workspace, TgWitness picks a pair from its built-in pool of 50 public API pairs ( tgwitness/api_pool.py ) in random order. If Telegram refuses a pair ( API_ID_INVALID , API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD , UPDATE_APP_TO_LOGIN ), the next one is tried, up to eight per sign-in; refused pairs are skipped until restart. The pair that signed in is saved with the account and reused for it. An API ID and API hash identify the application to Telegram; they do not authorize an account by themselves. To use your own application instead (the account that registers it is the one at risk; see Why a built-in API pool? ): Open my.telegram.org and sign in with any phone number you own. The code arrives in the Telegram app, not by SMS. Choose API development tools . Create an application: any title and short name (5–32 letters), platform Desktop . URL and description can stay empty. Copy App api_id (a number) and App api_hash (32 hexadecimal characters). In the panel, open API ID + Hash under the sign-in form. You can paste a single api_id:api_hash pair into API ID and both fields are filled. One pair can be used for all of your accounts. After a successful login it is saved, encrypted, in that workspace only and is never sent back to the browser. Three different credentials are involved: Secret Opens Where it lives Panel token The TgWitness web panel panel-token.txt in the data directory, or TGWITNESS_TOKEN API ID + hash Nothing by itself; identifies the app Built-in pair, imported settings, or your own app at my.telegram.org Account authorization The Telegram account Created by phone/QR login or brought in as a session If Telegram must be reached through a proxy, set it first under Account → Settings → Connection settings → Change connection rout

pages.title: Reference · Access and permissions
pages.description: Issue scoped access to accounts and chats, choose permissions, limit sessions and IP addresses, and withdraw access.
pages.keywords: access permissions scope token session IP expiry revoke admin console
pages.text: Give a reviewer access to one chat, an analyst permission to export a case, or an operator control of selected accounts. Each person gets their own token. The main panel token stays with the administrator. Account setup · Connection routes · Security model Two scopes, two different jobs # Collection scope decides what an account records: selected chats, a Telegram folder or the whole account. Access scope decides which of those recorded accounts and chats another person can see and use. Giving access does not join a Telegram chat, start collection or grant Telegram account permissions. An access can open selected workspaces, selected chats within them, all workspaces, or every account of an account group . All workspaces, including ones added later also covers future accounts. A group access also covers accounts added to that group later. Select workspaces explicitly when a case should stay limited to them. Give someone access # Sign in as the main administrator and open Access . Under Give someone access , enter a name you will recognize in the log. Choose the workspaces and, where needed, the individual chats. Select what this person may do. View is always included. Set the expiry, sign-in/session limits and allowed addresses as needed. Press Create access . Copy the token now: it is shown only once. Send the panel address and token privately. The recipient enters that token on the normal sign-in page; they do not need your main panel token or a Telegram session. Open the panel with the issued token in a separate browser session and check the visible chats and permitted actions before handing it over. Choose the permissions # For a text-only public demonstration, use Public showcase instead of ordinary reviewer access. It shows explicitly selected public channels, retained edits and deletions, and signed statistics, with author fields redacted and files closed at the API boundary. Create and verify a showcase . Permission What it allows view Read permitted chats, captured messages, profiles, files and filtered journal records. Always included. export Export permitted chat history and dossiers. Whole-workspace evidence exports require access to the whole workspace. sources Manage sources, snapshots and profile capture. Chat-limited access can act only on allowed chats; account-wide source discovery and scope settings stay closed. collect Start or stop a collector. Requires whole-workspace access because collection affects the account. interact Perform supported Telegram interactions within the access scope. Chat-limited access cannot use account-wide link previews. settings Change collection settings, timestamps, notifications, off-site copies and parameters. Requires whole-workspace access. account Sign in or out of Telegram and manage connection routes. Requires whole-workspace access. board.read Read Case Board notes only within the permitted workspace and chats. board.write Add bookmarks, highlights, slices, comments and open/review statuses. Also needs board.read . board.manage Manage collections, final team statuses and other participants' cards. Also needs board read/write. Permissions and scope are checked together. Ticking a permission does not open other chats or unlock a workspace-wide operation for a chat-limited access. For a parallel export, the access must cover the exported chat in every selected account. An issued access cannot create new accesses, manage other people's sessions or open the administrator console. Three useful setups # Person Scope Permissions Reviewer One case's recorded chats view Analyst preparing a handover The chats to investigate and export view , export ; add interact only if they should act through Telegram Collection operator Selected whole workspaces view , sources , collect ; add settings or account only when needed The Access form's starting presets also include Case Board: Reviewer can read, Analyst can read and write, and Operator can manage it. Presets remain editable, and exist

pages.title: Reference · Connection, proxies and data protection
pages.description: Authentication, automatic proxy pools, IP modes, fallback policy, external requests and secret storage.
pages.keywords: proxy mtproxy pool socks5 http route IP mode fallback api id hash network
pages.text: This document describes TgWitness 0.8.0 behavior and its limits. Authentication, source access, network connectivity and capture completeness are separate states. For sign-in steps, file formats, and multiple accounts, start with accounts and session formats . For event policies and restart behavior, see how collection works . Guided connection setup # In Connection , the administrator can choose This account , An account group or All accounts , then select a route. Review selection lists the affected accounts. Prepare and check tests the proposed route without changing the saved one. Apply checked connection checks again, pauses observation if necessary, saves the route and resumes observation that was already running. It never starts collection in a previously idle account. History downloads remain paused and can be resumed separately. Pause active exports before switching. Group changes keep accounts with their own route by default. Clear that option only when the preview lists the changes you intend. Application reports each account's result; it is not an all-or-nothing transaction across databases. A failed switch restores that account's previous settings. A failure to resume is shown explicitly. Previews expire after ten minutes and changes to connection settings or group membership require a new check. Route What TgWitness manages Direct Connections from the host; an external host VPN is not detected or enforced. VPN One full-tunnel WireGuard profile per account, carried by a local userspace SOCKS5 process. No host interface or driver is installed. My proxy SOCKS5, HTTP CONNECT or MTProxy credentials. A URL can fill the SOCKS5/HTTP fields. Selecting several accounts shares this entered proxy. Public MTProto The existing pool assigns Telegram routes. External requests are disabled until a separate suitable proxy is configured in the advanced settings. WARP A separate local tunnel for each selected account, with WARP registration and a WireGuard profile kept in that account's vault. The current-route check uses a fresh unauthenticated Telegram transport, not the account's session. For HTTP-capable routes it also requests Cloudflare's HTTPS trace through that route and displays its reported exit IP, country, WARP state and check time. The measured latency is the Telegram connection setup time, not an ICMP ping. WARP preparation fails unless the trace reports WARP active. These checks establish connectivity, not the authenticity or completeness of captured messages. A running local process alone is not a successful exit check. Portable WARP and WireGuard # This is an unofficial WARP integration using wgcf 2.3.1 and wireproxy 1.1.3 . The administrator explicitly accepts setup before the first download or WARP registration. Those setup connections go directly to GitHub and Cloudflare and reveal the machine's IP. Ordinary account traffic keeps its existing route until application. Cloudflare chooses the exit address and country; separate tunnels can share an exit address. Country selection, periodic IP rotation and a host-wide VPN kill switch are not provided by this feature. Supported helper downloads: Linux and macOS x86-64/ARM64, and Windows x86-64. Artifacts are checked against SHA-256 hashes bundled in the reviewed source, and cached executables are checked again before launch. No helper is added to PATH, installed as a system service, or given a public listener. All files live under the workspace's portable-routes/ directory and encrypted vault entries. The loopback SOCKS5 listener requires independently generated credentials. Private profiles and WARP account credentials are encrypted with the existing workspace vault. While running, the helper needs an owner-only plaintext config; it is removed on a normal stop. A host crash can leave this file behind in the owner-only data folder. This does not encrypt the disk or protect against its administrator. The supervisor closes the tunnel if the panel's parent pipe disappears

pages.title: Reference · Deployment
pages.description: Run TgWitness as a service on Windows, Linux, macOS or Docker, behind HTTPS, with backups and updates.
pages.keywords: server docker compose systemd launchd https caddy backup update
pages.text: English · Русский · Українська · Español · Português (Brasil) · Türkçe · العربية · فارسی · اردو · हिन्दी · Bahasa Indonesia · Tiếng Việt · 简体中文 Choose an installation # For the portable package, extract TgWitness-<version>-windows-amd64-portable.zip from GitHub Releases. Native Linux/macOS sh start.sh No; use systemd/launchd for background use. Docker on any supported host docker compose up -d --build --wait Yes, while the Docker daemon runs. Docker and OS services remain prerequisites. Native and portable installations use data/live inside their folder. Docker uses the tgwitness-data named volume at /data . These are separate installations until you deliberately migrate the complete data directory. Do not expect a new Docker container to discover native accounts automatically. The bundled panel needs no Node.js or frontend build. Run the launcher from your normal OS account; administrator/root privileges are not required by TgWitness. Windows: Start.cmd checks py -3 , then python , then the default per-user and Program Files install folders, and requires version 3.11 or later. If none works, it offers the automatic per-user installation described above. py -3 start.py also works. The portable package needs no Python at all. A distribution's older default Python must be replaced or supplemented with Python 3.11+. macOS: install a current Python 3.11+ distribution; do not assume an OS-provided interpreter meets the requirement. Use python3 start.py from the project directory. Docker: use Docker Engine/Desktop with Compose v2.20 or newer. Docker Desktop must use Linux containers on Windows. The container installs its own Python dependencies; the host does not need a separate Python installation. Local computer # Use Start.cmd on Windows or sh start.sh on Linux/macOS. scripts\Setup.cmd or sh start.sh --setup-only prepares the environment. The launcher installs dependencies on first use; later launches reuse the environment. Internet access is needed for setup and Telegram collection, but browsing existing records and creating exports work offline. Run python start.py --check after setup to inspect local dependencies, Ed25519, storage, key configuration and the listening address without starting a collector. Use --json for structured output. pages.text: TgWitness records what a connected Telegram account observes. The journal preserves those observations, their sequence, and the context supplied with them. It does not infer unseen actions from a missing message or from an account being connected. From login to a journal # For self-destructing photos and files，see Self-destructing media ． It explains the priority worker，saved and unavailable outcomes，and the limits of read-receipt blocking in the API collector． Diagram as text Authorize a user account → Select accessible groups and channels Select accessible groups and channels → Save event and attachment settings Save event and attachment settings → Start observation Start observation → Receive updates from the active client Receive updates from the active client → Apply source and event policy Apply source and event policy → Append a signed observation Append a signed observation → Review or export the journal Append a signed observation → Process any queued attachment Process any queued attachment → Append the download outcome Authorization, access to a source, a running collector, and complete delivery are different questions. A successful login does not grant access to every group. A connected transport does not establish that every relevant update arrived. Observation scope: chosen chats, a folder or the whole account # Sources → Observation scope decides which chats a workspace records. Mode Records New chats Chosen chats (default) Only the chats you add by hand Never added automatically Telegram folder Chats in one of the account's folders: chats included by name, plus the folder's categories (contacts, non-contacts, groups, channels, bots), minus its excluded chats and, if the folder says so, archived chats Matching chats are added as soon as they become active; chats you add to the folder in Telegram are picked up within an hour Whole account Every chat the account sees Every new chat, group, private chat or bot is added the moment its first update arrives Source types (channels, groups, private chats, bots) narrow the folder and whole-account modes. Chosen chats can be of any type, including private chats and bots. Excluded chats are never recorded, in any mode. In folder and whole-account modes, Exclude and Remove on a source put it on this list, so the scope does not add it again. Choosing the chat again by hand (in Sources or from Chats) takes it off the list. The list holds up to 5,000 chats; past that, Remove is refused and the chat can be paused instead. Own actions (on by default): messages this account sends, its edits and its reply-keyboard button presses. Turned off, outgoing messages and edits are skipped. Switching to a folder or the whole account asks for confirmation: these modes record private chats and messages of third parties and belong on a dedicated account only. The confirmation and every scope change are signed scope.changed records. Chats added by the scope appear as sources marked auto , recorded as scope.applied (at start and hourly) or source.discovered (a new chat while observing). Switching back to chosen chats pauses every automatically added source. What these modes cannot do: Secret chats are end-to-end encrypted between two devices and never reach TgWitness, in any mode. Nothing is recorded while TgWitness is not running. After a restart it asks Telegram for missed updates and rechecks chats, but Telegram does not return everything after long outages. Reports and verify.py show such periods as gaps (see coverage ). Only the first 1,000 dialogs are listed at start (the limit is under Parameters ); older chats are added when they next become active. The earlier history of an added chat is not fetched — take a history snapshot or a full chat export when you need it. Folder conditions that change all the time (muted, read) are not applied: such chats stay observed. Inline (callback) bot buttons pressed in another app are invisible to a second session; the bot's reply or edit is recorded.

A managed installation includes START-HERE.html and START-HERE.txt beside its launcher, with the repository link and commands tailored to its installation path. Run tgwitness guide --print over SSH, or tgwitness paths to locate the actual data directory. pages.text: Follow a case across channels, groups, private chats and bots, from initial acquisition to a cited timeline and verifiable handoff. The interactive website version is at /docs/cases/ ; preview instructions . Worked case: a destination changes across four conversations # An announcement points to a bot. An operations group discusses a new payment destination, and the bot's keyboard displays it. The announcement is edited, a private follow-up repeats the destination, and a group message disappears. The questions are: what was observed before and after the change, which Telegram accounts posted each item, where the destination appeared, which attachment bytes were preserved, and what intervals remain unknown? All names, IDs, times and journal references in this example are fictional. The workflow uses current features; the case map is an illustration, not an automatic graph generated by the application. Diagram as text Channels → Workspace journal Groups → Workspace journal Private chats → Workspace journal Bots → Workspace journal Workspace journal → Search all sources Workspace journal → People profiles with record references Workspace journal → Saved versions and attachment receipts Search all sources → Analyst timeline and source register People profiles with record references → Analyst timeline and source register Saved versions and attachment receipts → Analyst timeline and source register Workspace journal → Signed evidence ZIP Analyst timeline and source register → Case handoff with separately verified artifacts Signed evidence ZIP → Case handoff with separately verified artifacts 1. Define the case and collect the whole account # Connect the collecting account in its own workspace. In Case Board or your case register, record the case reference, account ID, workspace and observation start. Retain the trusted signing-key fingerprint independently. For a dedicated collecting account, open Sources → Observation scope → Investigation mode . The preset selects Whole account , channels/groups/private chats/bots, own actions, source profiles and the latest 200 visible messages for newly discovered sources. Review it, press Save scope , and complete the scope confirmation. Main accounts use selected chats or a folder; whole-account collection is available to accounts marked for investigation. Load chats and compare the sources with the account's dialog list. Check exclusions. Parameters → Chats read from the account's list defaults to 1,000 and allows up to 20,000. Sources beyond the list limit are added when they become active. Record what was actually enumerated. In Recording settings , select All visible activity and save the monitoring settings. Review attachment types/limits and free disk space. Start observation. Validate a controlled new message, edit and deletion, then retain the test references and any failures. Whole-account scope records account-visible activity within the saved settings. It does not access secret chats or automatically join every linked group. It also does not backfill every existing conversation. See collection scope . 2. Inventory every source and acquire historical context # Keep a source register with one row per chat: Field Record Identity Workspace, account ID, numeric chat ID, title and type Visibility Membership/role, access confirmed or unconfirmed, exclusions Live capture Start time, selected event types and later policy changes Journal history Snapshot requested/completed, limit, time and record references Full history Signed per-chat export filename, boundary and completion/failure Attachments Completed media receipts, hashes, sizes and skipped/failed outcomes Coverage Outages, incomplete intake, FloodWait, unavailable messages and other gaps Use the right acquisition for each source: Load full history in Sources loads available past messages from enabled sources into the workspace journal. It supports pause/resume and a signed progress report. See history acquisition . History snapshot sa

pages.text: Case Board gives an investigation team a shared working view of saved material. Bookmark an observation, highlight an exact passage, save a range of actions, and discuss it with colleagues. Cards retain their source references and signed revision history. Team annotations stay in the workspace, separately identifiable from the original Telegram observations. Evidence model · Access · Reports Work with a case # Open Investigation → Case Board in Standard or Expert mode. The language follows the panel. Use To board beside a journal record or saved chat message, or focus it and press B . The bookmark is added to Inbox in one click. Edit its title, labels and note, or move it to a collection. A changed card appends a signed revision; removing it preserves the history. For a first case, choose a collection and add the records that answer one question. Use comments to review the interpretation, then Presentation to walk through the cards and source context. Choose Case Board material separately in Report studio when preparing the deliverable. Saving a slice does not automatically configure a report's data filters. Select text inside a saved chat message to reveal Highlight → board . Select its colour and add a note. The server checks the exact quote and saved version, including emoji, RTL text and combining marks. The interface does not map a selection through masked or transformed text. Shift-click two records in one chat for Slice between , use Slice by time , or save the journal's current chat, period and event-kind filters. A saved slice has its own authoritative predicate: opening it in Journal also applies multiple chats, message-number limits and actor filters. Show records added since bookmark isolates the later additions. Changing Journal filters exits the slice. From People, Slice this person’s actions uses the recorded actor ID; it does not assume that the message author edited, deleted or reacted to a message. The slice dialog previews counts before allowing creation. all includes every recorded kind, including snapshots, edits, deletions, reactions, membership/service updates, own actions, buttons, media outcomes, recovered messages and future event kinds. The selection describes saved observations. Unknown-chat deletion notices are separate context, available only to a whole-workspace access, never attributed to one of the chosen chats. Collections have a declared chat scope. An empty scope means the whole workspace. A collection cannot contain cards outside its scope; a chat-limited participant cannot read a broader collection. Inbox is a virtual collection for unassigned cards. Search and filters cover visible cards only; threads and mentions inherit the parent card's access. Removed comments have a tombstone in the discussion. No viewer history is recorded. Presentation opens all cards in the chosen collection, with Card, Source context and Team comments views and keyboard Previous/Next controls. It provides no editing controls. The ordinary feed is paginated; presentation loads its list in pages and retrieves one card's detail at a time. Permissions # All operations require view , workspace/chat scope and board.read . board.write adds cards, comments, moves and open/review statuses. board.manage permits collection management, confirmed/dismissed statuses, revisions/removal of someone else's card. A status is a team decision, not a cryptographic verification result. Access form presets: Reviewer = read; Analyst = read/write; Operator = read/write/manage, in addition to their existing permissions. Existing grants do not silently acquire new rights. The main administrator has all rights, and posts as Main administrator . Use named grants for attribution. Mentions list only current accesses able to read the complete parent card. A grant for chat A cannot obtain a card or slice for A+B, even by guessing its ID or supplying a false target.chat_id . Target metadata is resolved from the signed event hash on the server. Col

pages.description: Report filters, eight designs, contents presets, saved change histories and the assessment included in signed exports.
pages.keywords: report configuration designs assessment trust verification signed PDF HTML
pages.text: Turn selected observations into a readable account of the case: its question, scope, saved changes, charts, findings and source references. Each report gives the recipient a way to check the delivered material and inspect its collection coverage. The Basis of trust and limitations section appears in journal, handover, chat, account and sharing reports. Journal and handover PDFs use the same assessment as their signed report.json . ZIP manifests carry case_assessment in the signed manifest. This assessment travels with the exported material. The original observations retain their existing signatures. Document formats and reading order # Report studio # Open Exports → Configure and preview . Work through Data → Design & contents → Preview : Use the whole workspace or choose chats, authors, inclusive UTC observation dates and event types. Load the catalog to search chats and authors, or enter their Telegram IDs. Author filters match recorded sender IDs; a deletion notice without a sender does not match an author filter. Pick a page design, then choose charts, participant labels, the transcript and your written findings. Changing the design keeps these choices. Build the preview. It shows actual counts, activity, participants, sample records, saved changes and missing message-number ranges. Changing a choice marks the preview out of date. Save before downloading HTML, signed PDF, signed JSON or the evidence ZIP. The data preview counts the complete stable journal prefix, not an initial sample. Only displayed sample rows and long lists are bounded; their omitted counts are shown. A later export takes a fresh stable snapshot, so ongoing collection may increase the figures. Scope, counts and source identity are included in the signed report. Opening or previewing the form does not save it. Choose the recipient's copy. Charts and the transcript use the selected records. Integrity, custody and coverage describe the full source journal. The evidence ZIP contains its original records and attachments. Use a minimized handover when a recipient should receive only selected, permitted data. Read edits, deletions and missing IDs # An edit shows the saved Before and After text and highlights the changed words. A deletion shows the last version saved before the notice. If no earlier content was captured, the report says so. When you select only edits or deletions, the preceding versions remain available as explicitly labelled context outside the filters. Unrelated messages are not added to these histories. Unobserved message IDs are gaps between known numbers in the chosen chats and date-derived ID span. Every known source record is checked before declaring a number unobserved: filtering out another author, an event type or a date cannot create a false gap. Neighboring saved messages are labelled as context. A missing number does not establish that a message existed or was deleted; deletion notices and unsuccessful rechecks remain separate event types. Choose a design # Eight page designs are available for journal and single-chat HTML and signed PDF reports. They use the same records and calculations, with different covers, typography, chapter headings, tables and spacing. Design Reading style Classic A traditional dossier with a dark cover and numbered sections. Editorial A framed serif title page, wide margins and a narrow chapter rail. Briefing A compact cover with a navy spine, short headings and close-set tables. Analytics A survey-style cover, modular chart plates and monospaced figures. Technical A ruled register, numbered reference rail and precise comparison tables. Overview A panoramic cover, generous spacing and prominent summary figures. Reading series A section rail and grouped chapters for findings, scope, changes and the observation journal. Ledger & margin Numbered chapters with a wide margin, exact chart tables and a separate message transcript. The design is saved per workspace and recorded in the signed export manifest. HTML

pages.title: Reference · Features and limits
pages.description: The current collection model, multi-account workflows, exports and operational boundaries of TgWitness.
pages.keywords: features product status collection accounts exports limits platform
pages.text: TgWitness preserves Telegram conversations accessible to connected accounts, records observed changes and prepares verifiable exports. This reference describes the collection model, current workflows and their boundaries. Standalone application # TgWitness has its own installation, data directory, and release lifecycle. The bundled web interface handles setup and review; exported records can be used independently. The operator connects their accounts, chooses sources visible to each, and obtains a saved observation journal. The panel exposes content, saved changes, observation provenance and known gaps. Another investigator can verify the exported material. The panel distinguishes account authorization, access to a source, collector activity and recorded coverage. Review those states together when assessing an interval with few messages or a connection problem. Shared investigations # An administrator can issue access tokens scoped to workspaces and individual chats, with per-action permissions, IP restrictions, expiry, sign-in limits and session control. A read-only reviewer can inspect a case without receiving Telegram authorization or the main panel key. Chat-limited access stays separate from account-wide settings and full-journal exports. Automatic MTProxy maintains working Telegram routes from four public sources or an operator catalog. IP modes determine whether failure must wait for another proxy or may use an explicitly permitted direct route. External HTTP requests have a separate route and off switch. Archive tools # History acquisition , archive search and analysis , read-only MCP , local OCR/transcription and outgoing webhooks are included in 0.7.1. Analytical reports and recognized text stay separate from captured events. Case Board adds source-linked bookmarks, quotes, notes and collections within a workspace. The report constructor selects material, sections and one of eight designs for supported HTML/PDF exports. Optional extras # Everyday setup is account → sources → observation. Extras is a separate destination with a Telegram witness bot and a GitHub capture preview. Each states its availability and requirements before showing settings. Choosing a card opens instructions; it does not enroll or start a service. Bot setup has three steps: create read-only access, choose publication settings, and launch on the witness host. Network and publication options, existing connections and verification commands are disclosed on demand. Downloaded configuration is distinct from a running witness. Switching extras retains the draft; account changes and locking clear the temporary token and form. The built-in guide includes launch instructions. GitHub Actions capture launches a pinned collector from your fork, captures one chat and produces an encrypted handoff with workflow provenance. Protocol and private sources # MTProto is Telegram's protocol; Telethon is the Python library TgWitness uses to speak MTProto. They are not alternative connection methods. Collection uses MTProto; the optional witness publishes signed checks through the Bot API. Each workspace has its own authorized client and account update stream. TgWitness selects observations from configured sources and makes separate explicit requests for functions such as history snapshots and media downloads. A private source needs no public username. Telegram peer type and numeric ID are the identifiers; titles and usernames can change. Access depends on existing membership and permissions. TgWitness does not automatically join sources or bypass join approval. An access hash from another account is not a universal access token. The collection model must account for pre-join hidden history, participant/admin roles, session revocation, removal or changed permissions, group-to-supergroup migration, topics/forums, linked discussions, channel identities and unavailable attachments. Not every combination has been qualified live. Source visibility is checked at collector

pages.title: Reference · How the evidence works
pages.description: Hash chain, signatures, checkpoints and witnesses explained with the exact formulas the verifier uses.
pages.keywords: hash chain sha256 ed25519 canonical json checkpoint formula
pages.text: TgWitness preserves what a collecting account observed, links those observations into a signed journal and lets another person verify an export against a trusted key and an earlier retained checkpoint. The local documentation website adds interactive examples at /docs/concepts/ , a checkpoint decision explorer at /docs/witness/ , and walkthroughs for Case Board , report design and handover extracts . All example messages, counts and delays are fictional. Hashes in the chain sandbox are calculated with SHA-256 in the browser. Nothing is sent to Telegram. A message changes; observations accumulate # Diagram as text Telegram → Collector: New message: Meet at 10:00 Collector → Signed journal: Append message.new Telegram → Collector: Edit: Meet at 11:00 Collector → Signed journal: Append message.edited Telegram → Collector: Deletion notice Collector → Signed journal: Append message.deleted Note on Signed journal: Original + edit + deletion observation remain This simplified sequence assumes Telegram delivered each update and the selected account could see it. Operational events also share the journal. A deletion notice does not supply the deleter or an exact deletion time. Repeated deliveries are separate observations; there is no journal-wide duplicate suppression. What a hash covers # Read the formula from the inside out: C turns the nine fields into exact bytes; SHA-256 produces their digest; hex is how that digest is stored. The previous hash is already inside the event. unhex turns the stored hash back into the 32 bytes that Ed25519 signs. Static chain diagram Let C(e i ) be the canonical UTF-8 JSON of the nine event fields. The first previous_hash is 64 zero characters. Each later record includes the preceding record's hexadecimal hash: h i = hex(SHA256(C(e i ))) σ i = Ed25519.Sign(sk,unhex(h i )) The signature covers the 32 raw digest bytes. The hash input contains exactly seq , observed_at , source_at , kind , chat_id , message_id , actor_id , payload and previous_hash . Object keys are sorted; whitespace and ASCII escaping are omitted; NaN and infinity are rejected. See the exact encoding . Diagram as text 64 zero characters → Record 1 / hash h1 Record 1 / hash h1 → Record 2 includes h1 / hash h2 Record 2 includes h1 / hash h2 → Record 3 includes h2 / hash h3 Record 3 includes h2 / hash h3 → Signed checkpoint: count 3, head h3 (retain elsewhere) Change to the supplied journal What detects it Alter record 2 while leaving its saved hash Recomputed event hash differs; its signature no longer covers the changed event Rebuild the altered record and every later hash The original signatures fail; a retained checkpoint at the affected boundary also disagrees Remove the tail but keep the remaining prefix intact An earlier retained checkpoint beyond the supplied prefix reveals that the export is too short Re-sign a replacement journal with another key A separately trusted key fingerprint rejects the replacement identity Try the logic on record 2: change Meet at 11:00 to Meet at 12:00 in the saved event. Its recomputed hash no longer matches. Recalculating the later chain can repair its links, but cannot make the original signatures cover the new digests. An observed Telegram edit, by contrast, becomes a new journal record. Static change diagram Hash links alone do not prevent someone from recalculating a replacement chain. Trust comes from checking signatures under an independently trusted key and comparing with references retained outside the collector. What an earlier checkpoint adds # The reference stays still while the journal grows. If the checkpoint says “3 records, head h3”, a four-record export can pass by matching h3 at position 3. Its newest head is h4, which is expected to differ. An export of only two records fails. Static checkpoint diagram After verifying the checkpoint signature, require: N export ≥ N checkpoint and h export [N checkpoint ] = H checkpoint An export may extend beyond a checkpoint. pages.title: Reference · Evidence format
pages.description: Contents of the signed ZIP, record kinds, process receipts, people profiles, off-site copies and offline verification.
pages.keywords: evidence zip manifest events jsonl verify dossier replica s3
pages.text: TgWitness preserves account-visible Telegram observations in a signed journal. Recipients can verify the saved records, attachments and reports against a trusted collector key, then compare the journal with an independently retained checkpoint. This page describes the formats, the checks and the material to keep for handover. What is signed # Material Protection What to retain Every journal observation, including operational events SHA-256 chain and an Ed25519 signature per event Original events.jsonl , the trusted key fingerprint, and a retained checkpoint Evidence ZIP contents manifest.sig signs the canonical manifest, which lists hashes of the content files The complete ZIP, including its manifest and signature Preserved attachments SHA-256 and byte count in a signed media.saved event; file hash in the signed ZIP manifest The original bytes inside the verified ZIP Checkpoint Ed25519 signature over journal length, head hash, public key, and creation time An independent copy retained before a disputed change Run receipt Signed record of the collector version，source-file hashes and start settings，also included in process.started The receipt，associated journal and the environment evidence for the selected verification mode Readable reports: report.html and its parts, report.json , report.pdf , chat.pdf An Ed25519 seal per file over its content; the PDF also carries a standard PDF signature (see Readable reports ) The file as received and the trusted key fingerprint; the ZIP it describes Standalone CSV No standalone cryptographic signature; event hashes alone are insufficient Use the exact copy inside the verified ZIP for integrity checking Screenshots, printouts, or PDF produced by a browser No TgWitness signature on the derivative Keep the original verified package and document how the derivative was made The collector verifies journal signatures before generating every export format. Readable HTML and PDF reports carry their own seals; standalone CSV is checked as part of a signed ZIP. Keep the ZIP to retain the attachment bytes and manifest, and a separate checkpoint to check the journal against an earlier boundary. Investigation handoff # Record the case reference, operator, numeric Telegram account ID, selected sources, collection policy, and collection period in your case notes. TgWitness preserves observations and supports source-linked notes and collections in Case Board . Keep transfer and custody records with your case materials. Check the intended collection setup with the live acceptance procedure . Retain the workspace's public-key fingerprint independently before relying on its exports. Save signed checkpoints outside the collector during collection. Record interruptions and the limits of the account's visibility. Export a signed ZIP and retain the signed run receipt. Use a checkpoint at or before the exported journal boundary. A later checkpoint can correctly reject an earlier export as too short. Exports include the full workspace journal, regardless of panel filters; review the material before sharing it. Have the recipient verify the ZIP with a trusted copy of the verifier and the independently supplied fingerprint/checkpoint. From a trusted checkout with its Python environment active: python -m tgwitness.verify evidence.zip --fingerprint TRUSTED_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 --checkpoint retained-checkpoint.json Successful output reports key_pinned: true and checkpoint_checked: true when both inputs are supplied and accepted. Preserve the verification result. For a handover requiring the final exported record to be witnessed, use `--witness witness.zip --witness-fingerprint TRUSTED_WITNESS_SHA256 --require-witness`. This refuses an export with an unwitnessed tail. See the [witness handover procedure](WITNESS.md#require-a-witnessed-export-boundary). Record the archive's SHA-256, export boundary, transfer date, sender, and recipient in your custody record. Keep the original package intact and work from copies. Share eviden

pages.title: Reference · Independent witness
pages.description: Run a witness with its own key and bot, publish signed checkpoints to a channel and check exports against it.
pages.keywords: witness bot channel checkpoint tgw1 verify continuity
pages.text: Export and verify · High assurance · Panel guide A witness retains signed checkpoints separately from the collector．It checks the collector's signature and journal continuity，signs the result with its own key，and publishes it to a Telegram channel．Run it on a separate server with read-only access to the collector's witness endpoint． Diagram as text Collector → Witness (signed checkpoint: record count + head hash) Witness → Witness journal, own key Witness → Telegram channel (signed post via its own bot) Evidence ZIP → verify.py Witness journal, own key → verify.py Telegram channel → verify.py (Telegram Desktop export or t.me/s page) What the witness gets, and what it does not # The witness has The witness never has A read-only witness token for one workspace The collector's Telegram session or API credentials Its own Ed25519 key and journal The collector's vault, signing key or panel token Its own Telegram bot token Message content: the head is a record count and a hash The token is created in Extras → Independent witness , shown once and stored only as a SHA-256. It opens exactly one endpoint, GET /api/witness/head , which returns a freshly signed checkpoint plus signed content-free collection counters and operational health. It cannot open the panel, read message content or change settings, and the panel token is not accepted there. Revoke a token on the same page. The collector records when a new witness key starts checking ( witness.seen ) and shows the last check per token; a witness that has not checked within 2.5 intervals is marked overdue. New witnesses send a random challenge on each poll; the capture statement echoes it under the collector signature. Counters are bound to the exact checkpoint and are included in signed witness posts. Legacy heads remain accepted by the standalone witness. Journal growth alone is never counted as a new message. What it checks and records # Every interval (10 minutes by default) the witness: fetches the head itself (the collector cannot push or skip it); verifies the collector's signature, the pinned collector key ( --collector-fingerprint , or the first key seen)，a nondecreasing count and an unchanged head at an unchanged count． Merkle inclusion and consistency proofs verify that a growing journal extends the retained checkpoint．Once continuity proofs have been used，removing them is rejected； appends a signed record to its own journal: witness.anchor with status ok , key_changed , rollback (fewer records than before), fork (same length, different head) or invalid (the answer failed verification), or witness.no_response when the collector did not answer; posts the result to the channel, signed, including "no answer" while the witness is running and can reach the Bot API. The post ID is recorded ( witness.posted ), a failed post too ( witness.post_failed ). A post looks like this; the last line carries the signed statement: TgWitness witness #42 · journal head Collector 3fa9c2d1e0b4a7f6: 18234 records Head 9b1f…c07e 2026-10-28T19:40:00.123+00:00 TGW1.eyJhdCI6…<statement>.<signature> Run a witness # You need a Telegram bot (create one with @BotFather), a channel where that bot is an administrator, and the collector's address reachable from the witness — over HTTPS outside a private network (see the HTTPS profile in deployment ). Open Extras → Independent witness → Configure in the panel. Three steps cover read-only access, your channel and interval, then launching the witness. Publication policy, optional HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy and custom Bot API address are under Advanced settings . The form downloads witness.json with this workspace's collector key pinned. Download the newly created read-only token with Save access file as witness-token.txt ; place it and a bot-token.txt created on the witness host beside that JSON. The collector never receives the bot token. Downloading does not start a service or publish a message. No hosted project witness is implicitly enrolled. python -m tgwitness.wit

pages.title: Reference · Timestamps
pages.description: RFC 3161 timestamps for signed checkpoints: what is sent to the authority and how a response is verified.
pages.keywords: rfc 3161 tsa timestamp authority nonce checkpoint
pages.text: TgWitness prepares RFC 3161 requests and verifies timestamp authority (TSA) responses. This manual procedure neither selects a TSA nor submits data; evidence mode does both on a schedule ( evidence format ). A prepared request is not yet a timestamp proof . What the proof binds # Diagram as text Account observations → SHA-256 chain and Ed25519 signatures SHA-256 chain and Ed25519 signatures → Signed checkpoint Signed checkpoint → Exact-byte hash and random nonce Exact-byte hash and random nonce → RFC 3161 request RFC 3161 request → Independent TSA Independent TSA → Signed TSA response Signed checkpoint → Verify data, nonce and explicit CA trust Signed TSA response → Verify data, nonce and explicit CA trust The collector signature binds records to its key. A trusted TSA response can establish that a particular checkpoint existed by the TSA's stated time. The checkpoint can then bind the journal prefix. This does not establish the time of each Telegram action or the truth of the captured content. Procedure # Retain the collector key fingerprint through a separate trusted channel. A key supplied only by the examined ZIP is insufficient to identify the collector. In Exports → Prepare timestamp request , download the selected workspace's request ZIP. Extract checkpoint.json , timestamp.tsq , SHA256SUMS and README.txt . Do not change the checkpoint bytes. Choose a TSA appropriate to the investigation. Submit timestamp.tsq using its documented method, with application/timestamp-query for an HTTP service. Save the original binary reply as timestamp.tsr , the endpoint, retrieval time and request outcome. The request contains a hash and nonce rather than messages; network metadata still reveals the request. Obtain the trusted root certificate independently of the reply, plus any intermediates required. A certificate in the reply does not become trusted merely because it is included there. From a trusted TgWitness installation, verify: python -m tgwitness.anchor verify --checkpoint checkpoint.json --request timestamp.tsq --response timestamp.tsr --ca trusted-tsa-root.pem Add --intermediates tsa-intermediates.pem or --openssl /path/to/openssl if needed. OpenSSL must support ts . On Windows the verifier also searches the standard Git installation. OpenSSL 3.5.9 was tested locally with a synthetic CA/TSA. Export a signed journal ZIP after the checkpoint so it includes that prefix. Verify using the independently known fingerprint: python tgwitness/verify.py evidence.zip --fingerprint TRUSTED_SHA256 --checkpoint checkpoint.json Preserve the ZIP, checkpoint, request, reply, certificate chain, verification results and handoff record outside the collector. Repeat verification at receipt. To prepare a request from a saved checkpoint: python -m tgwitness.anchor prepare checkpoint.json --out timestamp-request.zip Preparation canonicalizes JSON and includes the matching checkpoint in the archive. Use the checkpoint bytes from that archive for TSA verification, even if the input file had different whitespace. Verification boundaries # Check Current behavior Data SHA-256 of the exact checkpoint bytes must match the response Request With --request , the original query and nonce are verified TSA signature OpenSSL verifies the signature and chain to the explicit CA Collector signature Separately verified by the journal verifier with a pinned key Revocation No automatic OCSP/CRL retrieval Long-term validity No archival validation after certificate expiry Scheduled submission Evidence mode, off by default --request is technically optional, but omitting it prevents verification of the original nonce. For this full procedure, the result's request_checked must be true. Certificate verification follows the installed OpenSSL's rules and verification time. Long-term preservation needs a separate certificate/revocation evidence policy. A valid cryptographic signature is not automatically a qualified timestamp or a legal admissibility determination. pages.description: Threat model, access model, secrets at rest, network exposure, session imports and how to report a vulnerability.
pages.keywords: security threat model token vault fernet encryption report vulnerability
pages.text: This page describes access，storage and network protection in a local or server workspace． For collection on a GitHub runner or in an Intel TDX confidential VM，see the verification modes ，which add checks of the collection environment． Account connections，notifications，timestamps，off-site copies and witnesses have their own routing settings． Area In short Access Administrator key plus scoped access to accounts/chats, seven permissions and revocable sessions; localhost by default Secrets at rest Session, API pair, signing key and proxy settings are encrypted with Fernet Messages and media Stored unencrypted: use disk encryption and strict permissions Integrity SHA-256 hash chain and an Ed25519 signature on every record Local trust boundary The host administrator controls the workspace and its signing key；independent checkpoints retain an earlier journal boundary For vulnerability reports, see the security policy . Access model # The main panel token grants full control. Other people can receive their own scoped access : chosen workspaces and chats, permissions, expiry, IP restrictions, sign-in limits and revocable sessions. A chat-limited access cannot perform whole-workspace operations even if their permission is ticked. Workspaces share a process and do not isolate data from the host administrator. The panel listens on localhost by default. Browser sign-in exchanges an access token for a session credential; the browser sends it as a bearer token. It is kept in sessionStorage rather than an authentication cookie. Lock/sign-out clears the browser session. Closing a browser or ending a session does not stop collection. Issued tokens and session credentials are kept as hashes in the encrypted vault. Revocation ends the associated sessions; permission changes affect subsequent requests. Downloaded files cannot be recalled. The administrator can limit their own browser sessions too, but scripts using the main panel token directly retain full access and bypass those browser-session limits. Failed authentication is rate-limited by client address. IP restrictions use the address seen by the application; check reverse-proxy behavior before relying on it. Witness credentials remain separate read-only checkpoint/health credentials. Demo access # /api/demo-access is a deliberately unauthenticated bootstrap for an explicitly started, isolated synthetic demo. It issues a separate process-lifetime capability, never the real panel token or a TGWITNESS_TOKEN override. Issuance and use require a loopback peer and Host, no forwarded headers, and no cross-origin request. Additional workspaces or an authorized session disable this path. Live workspaces never issue the capability. The demo cannot connect accounts or change collection settings. Panel content and exports # The panel uses no external fonts, analytics, CDN resources, or embedded remote media. Telegram-sourced text is inserted as text, not HTML. Downloaded attachments are served as binary attachments. JSONL exports preserve original strings; HTML escapes them; CSV cells that could become formulas are prefixed with an apostrophe. Exports exclude authentication and signing secrets, but deliberately contain collected source metadata, identifiers, and possibly personal or sensitive content. Telegram access hashes and file references can occur in raw source metadata. Secrets at rest # Telegram API credentials，the session and signing key are encrypted with Fernet． For local messages and media，encryption is provided by the host's disk or volume； the workspace stores ordinary files．Exports can use a password-protected AES-256 ZIP， and off-site copies use AES-256-GCM． The vault key defaults to the protected data directory．Use an external master-key file below to store it separately．On Unix，new private-key files use mode 0600 and new data directories use 0700；on Windows，set the directory ACL for the service account and authorized administrators．Existing directory permissions are retained． External

pages.text: One Python process hosts the FastAPI panel and any number of isolated workspaces, each with a Telethon user-account client. SQLite holds an append-only signed event journal and mutable operational settings. An encrypted vault holds API credentials, the StringSession, and signing key. The frontend is plain bundled HTML/CSS/JavaScript: no Node build, CDNs, or runtime frontend downloads are needed. Optional browser and AyuGram recorders run in separate processes or containers . The tgwitness_capture package owns their event format, keys, artifacts, checkpoint API, independent witness and standalone verifier. It is bundled in the main wheel and can also be installed alone from addons/capture , without importing the collector. The main panel's capture_api.py and capture_connections.py provide administrator-only, workspace-scoped controls under /api/capture ; connection tokens live in the encrypted vault. No recorder or outbound request starts with the main process. Each explicit command verifies a fresh challenge against the pinned recorder key. Exports are verified before download and keep their original signature; they do not become Telegram message events. Collection sessions and proxy routes stay with each client. See the English Independent capture guide for deployment and trust boundaries. pages.text: Project · Quick start · Deployment Install with one command # The guided installer includes a private Python runtime. Use the same address for future installations: each publication updates the installer, hashes, signatures and build information together. Linux / macOS (Bash): curl -fsSL https://get.destroy.tools/install.sh | bash On an Ubuntu server, run as root to install a background service. On a desktop, run as your normal user. Windows (PowerShell or Command Prompt): powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://get.destroy.tools/install.ps1 | iex" No administrator is needed on Windows. The child PowerShell process leaves your terminal open with the result. Python and dependencies stay in the installation. On Ubuntu, choose This computer , Temporary HTTPS link or Own domain . The installer prints the panel address and access key. For a temporary link, open that HTTPS address in your browser and enter the key. With local access on a remote server, use an SSH forward from your computer ( ssh -L 8787:127.0.0.1:8787 user@server ) and open http://127.0.0.1:8787 . On macOS and Windows, the local panel opens in your browser; keep its terminal running. Sign in to Telegram in the panel and choose what to collect. pages.text: The panel separates three tasks: Task What it does Keep a backup Copy the signed journal, checkpoints, preserved files and queued exports to the configured S3 destination. Free local space Copy selected older attachments to S3 or an rclone cloud remote, read them back in full, verify the encrypted bytes, then remove the verified local copy. Keep an evidence copy Configure S3 Object Lock and check the returned retention status. The service must confirm the requested mode and date. Freeing space never deletes or rewrites the signed journal. Each attachment keeps its original SHA-256 and a recovery receipt. Optional gzip compression takes place before authenticated encryption. Cloud filenames do not contain Telegram names, chat IDs or original attachment names. One attachment may be up to 32 GiB. An upload response alone is not permission to delete a file. TgWitness downloads the complete encrypted object and verifies its size and SHA-256, saves the receipt, then checks the local bytes again immediately before removal. An upload failure, different readback or cancelled transfer leaves the local file in place. If an enabled evidence backup has not yet copied that file, removal also waits for it. When the disk is filling up # Attachment downloads already pause below Parameters → Attachments → free disk space (1 GiB by default), keeping their queue. Text observations continue. This does not depend on notification settings. Disabling notifications does not disable the download reserve or storage safeguards. For earlier intervention, enable Run automatically , choose Remove the local file to free space , and enable Start an extra offload pass when disk space is low . The optional rule starts below 5120 MiB free and continues in batches until 10240 MiB is free by default. Both thresholds are configurable. It uses the same destination, minimum file age, batch limit, full readback verification and evidence backup prerequisites as a manual pass. It never enables a destination on its own. Checks run every 30 seconds; an error or no progress delays another pressure pass for five minutes. The pressure state and retry time survive a restart. Scheduled passes still use their normal interval when the pressure rule is inactive. The panel shows free space, the packing reserve, whether the pressure rule is armed, and files skipped for lack of temporary space. Packing and restoration check their peak temporary-space requirement before starting and check available space while writing. The reserve is the configured download reserve, with a 64 MiB minimum for storage operations. These checks are not a filesystem quota; another process can still consume space between checks. Gzip compression is lossless and applies to remote objects; it does not shrink the active journal or create local archives. JPEG/video/ZIP files may barely shrink or grow slightly. The current packing pipeline may temporarily need approximately twice the attachment size plus the reserve when compression is enabled. Choose a start threshold early enough for your largest files. A file too large to prepare is kept and reported; smaller files and previously verified remote copies can still free space. A verified copy can be offloaded without another local packing file. Restoration also needs temporary space and can be refused until space is available. If nothing eligible can be moved, or no destination is configured, TgWitness cannot reclaim space automatically. The signed journal is never pruned or rewritten by storage management. It still needs space for new text observations. Connect a destination # In Extras → Storage & disk space → Manage storage , choose the task and destination, save it, then select Test upload & download . The test uploads a small random probe and reads it back. It does not use Telegram content. For S3, use the provider's actual endpoint, region and bucket. Wasabi, Backblaze, Cloudflare R2 and other compatible services use the same S3 settings. A compatible API

pages.title: Reference · Account export
pages.description: Export what an account can read now: scope, resumable jobs, a signed archive and minimized sharing copies.
pages.keywords: account export takeout disclosure minimized sharing copy scope
pages.text: An account export reserves its account exclusively. Pause monitoring or another acquisition explicitly before starting or resuming; the app never stops it automatically. As the installation administrator, choose Start here → Export my account , or Exports → Telegram account → Configure account export . Sign in if needed, review the scope, and explicitly start the export. Continuous observation is not required. Saved observations is a separate export of the existing journal; its ZIP includes all sources regardless of journal filters. Every workspace has its own jobs, signing identity and storage. Issued panel access, including an unrestricted ordinary export grant, cannot open these account-wide routes. Sender and text filters expand under Filter by sender or message text . Account data & connection method contains optional account categories and the Takeout/regular-session choice; its summary shows the active choices even when closed. Closing these sections keeps their settings. Export and report drafts remain in the current panel session while changing views; they are not saved through a browser reload. Existing jobs remain reachable from either export choice. This workflow exports data currently accessible to the connected account. The default uses Telegram Takeout ; it is not a backup of unavailable or deleted Telegram data. Secret Chats, inaccessible history and earlier edits are not recovered. Telegram can impose a waiting period before Takeout starts. The panel displays that wait; it does not silently switch transport. The explicit regular-API option has different coverage and records unsupported categories. Choose what is collected # Setting Meaning Purpose Record why this acquisition is needed. Do not put unnecessary names or sensitive case details here. Report language Choose the language of the readable report's labels. Original message text remains unchanged; untranslated template labels use English. The language is fixed with the signed job options. Chat kinds / chat IDs All selected kinds, or just the listed chats; Saved Messages belongs to private chats. Archived chats are separately selectable. Dates UTC. The panel's From and Through calendar dates are both included. The API uses inclusive from_utc and exclusive to_utc ; the panel sends the start of the day after Through. An empty bound leaves that side unrestricted. Sender IDs Only messages by the listed senders; an empty list includes all senders. Text contains Case-insensitive literal phrases, matched with OR. Sender/date/own-message conditions combine with AND. Own messages Keep only outgoing messages. Media types Select attachment categories, or clear all to avoid downloading message files. File / total media limits Per-file MiB and total downloaded-media GiB. Text, receipts, readable reports and ZIP overhead require additional disk space. Account categories Profile, contacts, profile photos, stories, session metadata and other Takeout data have separate controls. The Minimize collection preset disables files and account metadata. Sender/content filters apply before retained message pages and media downloads. Telegram still transmits API history pages containing messages needed to evaluate those filters: filtering is not a promise that unselected messages never enter process memory. Other ongoing observation in the workspace has its own scope and retention settings. Profile-photo history and stories are not selected by default. Disable profile and contacts as well when the case needs messages only. If attachments or metadata are unnecessary, excluding them during acquisition avoids retaining another private copy in this export. Photo payloads use the still-image variant identified in their metadata and hash manifests，including photos with an animated avatar variant．That animation is not substituted for the selected still image．A shorter or longer payload than the observed size is recorded as a failed attachment，and a changed representation during file-refer

pages.title: Reference · Public showcase
pages.description: Publish saved messages of selected public channels and signed snapshots through expiring, revocable links.
pages.keywords: showcase public channel link snapshot redaction verify
pages.text: Access → Public showcase creates a separate, read-only page using the existing access-token system. It reads the installation's saved observations. It does not start a collector, sign in to Telegram or acquire a channel for a visitor. Publish a page # Save a source profile for each public channel you want to show. A channel must have a public username in its latest saved profile; groups and private chats are not eligible. Open Access → Public showcase (or /showcase-manage.html ) as the administrator. Select channels across up to 16 workspaces, enter the public page title, and choose a link lifetime of 1, 7 or 30 days. Internal workspace labels are not published. Up to 64 channels can be included. Review the selected channels' text for publication, then click Preview selected records . The preview uses the same server-side projection as the visitor page. Click Create showcase link . Copy the link while it is visible. Open it in a separate browser to review the recipient's page before distributing it. The link contains an access token in its URL fragment. The page removes the fragment before making API requests and exchanges it for a browser session. Anyone holding the link can open the selected material until expiry or revocation. New links allow 100 concurrent sessions, each lasting at most one hour. Existing Access controls can also enforce address restrictions and sign-in limits through the grant API. Normal reviewer access is a different mode and still includes the original permitted messages and files. What visitors see # Visible Kept private Selected public channel titles, usernames and profile observation dates Account identities, internal workspace labels and unselected sources Captured text and each saved edit Structured sender IDs, names, usernames, phone numbers and profile values Deletion observations with the previously saved text, if available Attachments, avatars, thumbnails, filenames and original payloads Markers saying an author/profile or attachment was recorded Forwarding and reply metadata, network routes, IP addresses and credentials Selected-channel event counts, current collection switches, heartbeat and checkpoint interval Collection controls and ordinary evidence-export APIs Signing fingerprint, journal checkpoint and consistency proof Signing keys and Telegram sessions Public message text is not automatically anonymized. A name, mention, phone number or link written into the message remains part of that text. Redacted applies to the structured author/profile fields. Review the actual selected content before publishing it, including preserved edits and deletions. Eligibility reflects the latest saved source profile , not a live Telegram lookup. If a subsequent profile no longer has a public channel username, new requests exclude the channel. Refresh source profiles when public visibility changes. Readers may already have saved material they previously received. The original signed records stay unchanged. The displayed projection is signed separately and carries hashes referencing its original records. A projection signature authenticates the displayed statement; it is not the original event's signature over redacted bytes. Check signatures and continuity # Expand Fingerprint & signed checkpoint and download a snapshot. After a page refresh, the download includes the preceding browser snapshot and a Merkle consistency proof between their journal boundaries. Automatic refresh is once a minute while the page is visible and showing its first page of observations. With TgWitness installed, verify the downloaded file offline: python -m tgwitness.showcase_verify showcase.json --fingerprint TRUSTED_COLLECTOR_SHA256 The fingerprint must come from a separately trusted reference. To compare against a snapshot you retained yourself, use --previous earlier.json ; this overrides the previous snapshot carried inside the download. pages.title: Reference · High-assurance deployment
pages.description: A sealed 24/7 server on Hetzner or Phala Cloud, Gateway DNS and the checks a third party can repeat.
pages.keywords: high assurance hetzner phala tdx cloudflare gateway dns sealed server
pages.text: High-assurance deployment adds independent checks of the collection environment to archive verification．The reviewer queries deployment and access records held by the cloud provider and Cloudflare，and an Intel TDX deployment adds hardware attestation of the collector's environment． Ordinary local and Docker use is unchanged. Nothing here runs unless you deploy with python -m tgwitness.cloud , and the collector reads its host only when the deployment sets TGWITNESS_ASSURANCE . Diagram as text Operator → Server, firewall without inbound rules (provider API) Operator → Tunnel and DNS (Cloudflare API) Server, firewall without inbound rules → Tunnel and DNS (outbound only) Server, firewall without inbound rules → Signing key created on the server Verifier, read-only tokens → Provider log and firewall Verifier, read-only tokens → Tunnel connector address and ingress Verifier, read-only tokens → Signed /api/assurance statement Verifier, read-only tokens → Evidence ZIP What a verifier can check # Claim How it is checked Kept by The server was created through the provider API at a known time Server object and its creation in the provider's own log Provider Nobody used the provider's access paths Log of console requests, rescue, password reset, rebuild, ISO, images, backups Provider Nothing could connect to it The provider firewall has no inbound rules; SSH is masked from the first boot Provider (firewall), host (SSH) The panel is reached only through the tunnel Tunnel ingress forwards to the panel alone; the connector runs from the server's address Cloudflare This exact software runs The collector's signed source-tree hash equals a checkout of the deployed commit Collector, checked against Git The signing key was created on that server The key signs a statement naming the provider's server ID and the hash of the cloud-init it received Collector, checked against the provider The journal belongs to that key and server Every process start in the evidence ZIP carries the host measurement for that server Evidence ZIP The collector records SSH state，sessions，login history and boot information in signed process-start and host.state records．On an ordinary VM these are local inventory records，which the reviewer compares with the provider's independent records．The Intel TDX deployment below additionally verifies hardware-backed measurements． Providers # Credentials are read from --provider-token-file or the variable above, never from the command line. For AWS the file holds ACCESS_KEY_ID SECRET_ACCESS_KEY [SESSION_TOKEN] ; the region is --location . What each provider's records cannot show is printed in every report. In short: Hetzner logs console requests; DigitalOcean's Recovery Console, Linode's Lish/Glish and Vultr's web console are not logged as such, so root is locked at the first boot and a console login would need a password reset or a boot change, which are logged.
